author: ajac-zero
body:
**Description**

The `prefix` field on `VersionedAPISchema` is accepted by the CRD for any schema, but until now it was silently dropped for the Anthropic backend (the request path was hardcoded to `/v1/messages`). This wires `prefix` through `schemaToFilterAPI`, the filter API config, the endpoint spec, and the `anthropicToAnthropicTranslator` so users can route to Anthropic-compatible backends served under a custom prefix (e.g. `/gateway/v1/messages`).

Default behavior is unchanged: when `prefix` is unset the controller defaults it to `"v1"`, preserving today's `/v1/messages` request path.

`AWSAnthropic` and `GCPAnthropic` still ignore the field. The CRD doc comment is updated accordingly.

This change was developed with assistance from Claude Opus 4.7, with all code reviewed and tested by me.

author: philtim
body:
## Summary

Replace the tag-triggered \`release.yml\` with one that fires on push-to-main whenever \`package.json\`'s \`version\` field changes.

The workflow:
1. Checks out HEAD plus one prior commit.
2. Diffs the \`version\` field — skips the run if it's unchanged (e.g. when a PR only bumped dependencies).
3. Builds + packages via \`npm run deploy\`.
4. Creates and pushes the \`vX.Y.Z\` tag (skipped if it already exists, so re-runs on the same commit are idempotent).
5. Uploads the ZIP as a GitHub release asset with auto-generated release notes.

To cut a release: bump \`version\` in \`package.json\` on a feature branch, merge to main. No manual tag push needed.

README documents the flow.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML lints (CI on this PR will run \`ci.yml\` as usual since no version change).
- [ ] After merge, bump version on a tiny follow-up PR — release should auto-publish.

author: soulware
body:
## Summary

Two-commit stack continuing the orchestrator-style cleanup of the GC code paths started in #243.

### `6eac190` extract GcCycleOrchestrator from per-volume tick body

Mechanical extraction of the per-volume drain + GC tick body from `run_volume_tasks` into a dedicated `GcCycleOrchestrator` in a new `elide-coordinator/src/gc_cycle.rs`.

- `run_volume_tasks` retains startup (prefetch, watch publishing, `PrefetchEntryGuard`) and the `evict_rx` / `tick.tick()` select arms. Each tick resolves to one `orch.run_tick().await` returning `TickOutcome::{Continue, Stop}`.
- `GcCycleOrchestrator::run_tick` performs precheck → snapshot lock → `run_volume_compactions` → `run_drain` → (if interval elapsed) `run_handoff_cleanup` → `run_gc_pass`. Same call order, same logs, same `last_gc` update semantics:
  - drain failure: `last_gc` unchanged, retry next tick
  - `gc_checkpoint` returns `None`: `last_gc` advances (idle pass)
  - successful gc: `last_gc` advances
- Stages stay private. The snapshot-lock guard's lifetime is scoped to a single `run_tick` so exposing stages publicly would require leaking that lifetime through the API.
- Cross-tick state (`last_gc`, `gc_was_active`) lives on `&mut self`. Per-tick scratch (`drain_ok`, `u_gc`, the guard) stays as locals.

`tasks.rs` shrinks from 657 → 449 lines; `gc_cycle.rs` adds 315.

### `6eac190` extract load_pass_state + select_bucket; HandoffCursor

Two extractions inside `gc.rs`, no behaviour change.

`gc_fork` (240 → 54 lines): the body splits into `load_pass_state` (vk + ancestor walk + extent index + lbamap + WAL replay + collect_stats + deferred-partition + log) returning a `PassState`, and `select_bucket` (dead/small/large partition + sparse-large filter + tiered bin-pack + skip-check + per-pass log) returning a `SelectionOutcome` that's either `Compact(PackedBucket)` or `NoCandidates`. `gc_fork` keeps the early bail-outs (NoIndex, PendingHandoffs), the stale-file cleanup, and the final `compact_segments` call — composing the result `GcStats` from `PassState`'s `total_segments` / `deferred_count` and the outcome's packed accounting.

`apply_done_handoffs` (139 → 46 lines): `collect_bare_handoffs` extracts the read_dir + filter + sort. `HandoffCursor` carries the per-pass resources (`vk`, `volume_ulid`, `cache_dir`, `store`, `part_size_bytes`, `fork_dir`, `volume_id`) — loaded once after we've gated on a non-empty bare set, instead of reloading `vk` every iteration. `process_one` returns `Result<bool>` so the caller's `count` increments cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p elide-coordinator --tests` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p elide-coordinator --tests -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo test -p elide-coordinator --lib` — 231 passing
- [x] `cargo test -p elide-coordinator --bin elide-coordinator` — 92 passing
- [ ] CI runs the kernel lane against the full suite

author: anneschuth
body:
## Summary

Two new auto-approved MCP tools that extend the bot's read scope from the current thread out to any in-scope channel.

- **`read_channel_history`** — read recent messages in a channel by id. Use when the user asks about activity in another channel, or when investigating context outside the current thread.
- **`search_messages`** — search across the platform, with results filtered to in-scope channels. Mattermost only — Slack returns an explicit error pointing at the missing user token.

## Scope rule (unchanged from #371)

Bot's own channel (any visibility) ∪ any public channel on the same instance.

- Mattermost: \`getChannelInfo\` + post-filter on \`channelType\`
- Slack: bot must be a member of the target channel (Slack's API can't see channels the bot isn't in). Surfaced explicitly: "bot is not a member of that channel — invite it before reading history."

## Search result filtering

Mattermost search has no public-only flag, so the handler post-filters every match: keep it iff \`channelId === botChannel || channelType === 'public'\`. Posts where \`channelType\` is undefined are treated as private (fail-safe), matching the existing \`read_post\` resolver behavior.

The handler over-fetches by 2× (capped at 50) so the in-scope filter doesn't starve the result set when private matches are dropped.

## Tests

20 new tests across happy paths, scope rejection, shape rejection (channel id regex), search filter correctness, fail-safe behavior, platform-error pass-through, and Slack/Mattermost asymmetries. RED-GREEN verified on three load-bearing guards:

- In-scope predicate in \`read_channel_history\`
- Post-filter in \`search_messages\`
- Channel-id shape regex (Mattermost 26-char, Slack \`[CGD]\` + uppercase alphanumeric)

## Test plan

- [ ] Mattermost: \`read_channel_history\` on the bot channel id, confirm history returns
- [ ] Mattermost: \`read_channel_history\` on a public channel id on the same instance, confirm history returns
- [ ] Mattermost: \`read_channel_history\` on a private channel the bot isn't in, confirm rejection
- [ ] Mattermost: \`read_channel_history\` with a malformed id (URL paste), confirm shape error
- [ ] Mattermost: \`search_messages\` for a term that exists only in a private channel, confirm zero results
- [ ] Mattermost: \`search_messages\` for a term in the bot channel and a public channel, confirm both returned
- [ ] Slack: \`read_channel_history\` on the bot channel, confirm it works
- [ ] Slack: \`read_channel_history\` on a channel the bot isn't in, confirm "not a member" error
- [ ] Slack: \`search_messages\`, confirm explicit user-token error

author: dylan-conway
body:
Fixes #156.

`ripgrep` is used by `linuxGetMandatoryDenyPaths()` to expand glob deny patterns into concrete paths for bwrap. The macOS path never invokes it — seatbelt profiles take regex patterns directly (the existing `// no ripgrep needed on macOS` comment in `macos-sandbox-utils.ts` already says as much).

`checkDependencies()` was checking for `rg` unconditionally, so on a macOS host without `rg` on `PATH`, `SandboxManager.initialize()` throws

```
Sandbox dependencies not available: ripgrep (rg) not found
```

even though `rg` is never used there.

Moves the check inside the `platform === 'linux'` branch and adds tests covering both platforms.

## Summary
- Fixes #390. The `/v1/telemetry` endpoint (`TelemetryCollector` singleton) ignored `HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off` because it consulted a different env var (`HEADROOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, undocumented). The Supabase beacon honoured the documented var, so users had two telemetry systems with different opt-out behaviour and no way to disable the endpoint short of finding the undocumented one.
- Collector now calls `is_telemetry_enabled()` (the same predicate the beacon uses). Both env vars take effect; `HEADROOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` stays accepted for back-compat.
- Drive-by: two pre-existing `isinstance(v, (int, float))` UP038 violations in the same file converted to `int | float` so the pre-commit ruff hook stops complaining on every commit that touches the file.

body:
## Summary

- Generalize `OllamaPackageTrustPolicy` for the macOS Ollama package: `DefaultMacPackage` pinned to v0.5.7 (matching Windows), shared validator core for both platforms, and a Mac trust attestation under `mac/tools/ollama/ollama-package-trust.json`. Apple Silicon (arm64) Mach-O slice check runs in pure managed code so Windows-side PrepApp can verify staged Mac payloads without `lipo`.
- New `MacOllamaLifecycleService` in `runner-core/` (plain `net8.0`): implements `IOllamaLifecycleService` against `mac/tools/ollama/ollama`, gates `Start` on the Mac trust validator, sets `OLLAMA_MODELS` / `OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1` / `OLLAMA_ORIGINS`, and uses `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` for `serve` (never string-concat).
- PrepApp staging now hash-verifies, arm64-validates, and writes the Mac trust attestation via a small `MacOllamaStagingPipeline` helper; failures scrub the partial directory and refuse to stage. `PrereqFetch` is repinned to the same v0.5.7 release so CI, the bundled zip, and the runtime gate stay in lockstep.
- Swift `mac-runner` re-checks the on-SSD attestation at every launch and refuses to start `ollama serve` on missing / malformed / URL-mismatched / SHA-mismatched attestations. Existing encrypted-config-locked behavior is preserved (MAC5 territory).

## Files

Implementation:
- `shared/OllamaPackageTrustPolicy.cs` — `DefaultMacPackage`, `PinnedMetadataByUrl` entry, `GetMacTrustAttestationPath`, `WriteMacTrustAttestation`, `ValidateMacExecutionAttestation`, `ValidateArm64Slice`, shared `ValidateExecutionAttestationCore` extracted from the Windows path.
- `shared/MachOArchInspector.cs` (new) — pure-managed Mach-O / fat-Mach-O parser.
- `shared/MacOllamaStagingPipeline.cs` (new) — coordinated verify-then-attest helper used by `ArtifactStagingService` and tests.
- `shared/Prereqs/MacToolCatalog.cs` — pinned URL aligned with `DefaultMacPackage`.
- `runner-core/Services/MacOllamaLifecycleService.cs` (new).
- `prep-app/Services/ArtifactStagingService.cs` — wires the pipeline into the Mac staging path.
- `tools/FreeAiSsd.PrereqFetch/Program.cs` — pins Mac fetch to v0.5.7.
- `mac-runner/Sources/main.swift` — Swift trust gate.

Tests:
- `tests/MacOllamaTrustPolicyTests.cs` (new) — Mac attestation path: missing, malformed, URL mismatch, digest mismatch, happy path; Mac/Windows attestations co-exist independently; arm64 slice validator covers x86_64-only, universal, pure-arm64, and missing-binary cases.
- `tests/MachOArchInspectorTests.cs` + `tests/MachOFixtures.cs` (new) — parser exercises thin/fat (32 + 64), x86_64-only and arm64+x86_64 fat universal binaries, and refuses Java class files that share the `0xCAFEBABE` magic.
- `tests/MacOllamaLifecycleServiceTests.cs` (new) — path resolution, refusal when binary missing, env-var setup via `BuildStartInfo`, and trust validation interplay.
- `tests/MacOllamaStagingPipelineTests.cs` (new) — happy path writes attestation, refuses on hash mismatch, refuses on missing-arm64 binary, refuses on missing binary; no attestation is written on any failure mode.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI `windows-build` job (`dotnet build` + full `dotnet test` on net10.0 test host).
- [ ] CI `mac-runner-build` job (`swiftc` build of `mac-runner/Sources/main.swift`); locally `swiftc … -typecheck` is clean.
- [ ] `MacPlatformBoundaryTests` still passes (`runner-core` remains plain `net8.0`, non-WPF, non-Windows-targeted, no blocked Windows-only packages).
- [ ] Manual smoke (cannot run from this environment, called out as gaps): real-Mac launch with a tampered / deleted attestation should refuse; real-Mac launch with a clean attestation written by Windows PrepApp should succeed; staging an x86_64-only Mac payload should refuse with `Arm64SliceMissing`.

## Notes

- Did not modify Windows Ollama lifecycle behavior or the encrypted-config format.
- Did not bypass `OllamaPackageTrustPolicy` for any path — extended it.
- Did not check the downloaded `ollama-darwin.zip` into the repo. Pinned SHA-256 (`09ad6bb2…9971`) and URL only.
- MAC5 (encrypted config unlock on Mac) and MAC6 (Mac LAN API host) are not started here.

🛡️ Sentinel: [security improvement] Prevent localized DoS in Text Inputs

🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** Missing `maxLength` properties on React Native `TextInput` components (search fields, journal entries) allow for infinitely long input strings.
🎯 **Impact:** Exceedingly large inputs can lead to localized Denial of Service (DoS) due to memory exhaustion, UI freezing, or quota issues when saved to AsyncStorage.
🔧 **Fix:** Explicitly set sensible `maxLength` limits on `TextInput` components (`maxLength={5000}` for journal entries, `maxLength={100}` for search queries).
✅ **Verification:** Verified that tests pass and the changes are correctly reflected in the codebase without breaking UI logic.

author: skovtun
body:
## Summary

Wk1 #3 of Tool 1. Implements RFC 9309-compliant robots.txt check before each extract navigation. Per design doc constraint: \"honor target-site robots.txt before extraction (skip if disallowed)\".

**Default ON.** Pass \`honorRobotsTxt: false\` in ExtractOptions to opt out.

## What's added

\`packages/core/src/url-extract/robots-check.ts\`:
- \`defaultRobotsCheck(url, opts)\` — fetches \`<origin>/robots.txt\`, parses for matching UA group, applies rules. Returns \`{ allowed, reason, matchedRule? }\`.
- \`parseRobots(body, ua)\` — User-agent groups, specific-UA-overrides-wildcard, multi-UA group sharing, comments stripped.
- \`matchPath(path, rules)\` — longest-match-wins, Allow > Disallow on tie (per RFC §2.2.2).
- \`patternMatches(path, pattern)\` — \`*\` wildcard, \`$\` end anchor, regex metachars escaped (no injection vulnerability).

Wire-in (\`browser-capture.ts:captureSnapshot\`): runs robots check after SSRF guard, before \`page.goto\`. Throws \`ROBOTS_DISALLOWED\` distinct error class on block. Robots.txt URL itself runs through the same SSRF guard.

## Fail-open by design

RFC 9309 §2.4: missing robots.txt = allowed. Network errors, 4xx, timeouts, malformed bodies all treated as no-robots-txt. Blocking on unavailability would let any flaky origin DoS extraction by simply not serving robots.txt.

## Scope limits (intentional)

- UA matching is case-insensitive substring — no UA-token wildcards
- Crawl-delay, Sitemap, Host directives ignored (not relevant to extract)
- Specific UA group fully overrides \`*\` group when matched (RFC §2.2.1)

## Stats

- 30 new tests (1959 total, +30 vs main)
- 26 robots-check unit tests (parser/matcher/fail-open edge cases)
- 4 captureSnapshot wire-in tests (allow, block, opt-out, default-on)
- TS clean, prettier clean, build clean (DTS too)

## Test plan

- [x] vitest 1959/1959
- [x] TypeScript clean
- [x] Prettier clean
- [x] tsup build + DTS clean
- [x] Disallow: / blocks navigation
- [x] Allow: /public + Disallow: / → /public allowed
- [x] honorRobotsTxt: false skips check entirely
- [x] Network failure → fail-open
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm UA \`CoherentExtractBot\` is the right default identifier
- [ ] Reviewer: any concern about UA-token wildcards being unsupported?

## Notes

- Independent of PR #91 (token-normalizer) and PR #92 (fixtures). All 3 can land in any order.
- Default ON is the safer / spec-compliant default for a tool that fetches third-party sites.

author: thytran1402
body:
**Motivation**
The collector watcher ingests `metadata.yaml` files from upstream with no version identifier on the schema. When the upstream schema evolves; the parser silently drops new fields or misreads restructured data. There is no local copy of the upstream schema stored, so drift is undetectable without manually diffing the live URL, and no automated alert exists when it happens.

**Issue Resolved**:
- #40 

**Approach**
1. Schema snapshot: copy `metadata-schema.yaml` from the cloned opentelemetry-collector repo into ecosystem-registry/collector/meta/v{version}/ once per release. Stored distribution-independently since the file lives in the core repo and applies to both core and contrib.
2. Schema fingerprinting: annotate every generated component YAML with a schema_hash field (12-char SHA-256 of the raw schema bytes). This let backfill jobs and future consumers identify which schema generation produced a given file without inspecting the schema itself.

**Changes**
File: collector_watcher/schema_copier.py
Change: `CollectorSchemaCopier.copy_schema()` and `compute_schema_hash()`

File: collector_watcher/collector_sync.py
Change: `save_version()` computes hash, passes it to inventory, copies schema to `meta/` for core only

File: collector_watcher/inventory_manager.py
Change: Added meta_schema_path(version); `save_versioned_inventory()` writes `schema_hash`; `load_versioned_inventory()` defaults to "unknown" for backward compat

File: collector_watcher/metadata_parser.py
Change: `BaseMetadataParser`, `MetadataParserV1`, `MetadataParserFactory`, `parse_component_metadata()`; `MetadataParser` wrapper unchanged from the caller's perspective

File: .github/workflows/nightly-registry-update.yml
Added Detect collector schema drift, Open or update schema drift issue, Close schema drift issue if schema is stable steps

File: tests/test_schema_copier.py: 11 tests
File: tests/test_metadata_parser.py: Extended: factory, V1, convenience function, auto-detection    
File: tests/test_inventory.py: Extended: `schema_hash` round-trip, backward compat, `meta_schema_path` 
File: tests/test_collector_sync.py: Extended: hash absent/present, schema copied to `meta/`, not duplicated in distribution dir 

**Testing**
- 135 tests pass 
- Verify `schema-drift` label exists in the repository 
- Trigger a manual `workflow_dispatch` run of the nightly workflow to confirm drift detection runs without error
- Confirm `ecosystem-registry/collector/meta/` is populated after the next nightly run

author: oznakash
body:
## What

Two operator-driven cleanups in one PR:

1. **Strip personal info from the legal docs** — drop the operator's name and personal email, route contact through a project mailbox (`learnai@useyl.com`).
2. **Switch the browser-tab favicon to EmDash** — so the icon shows up consistently in the tab too, not just on iOS home screens / LinkedIn / `/icon-400.png` directly.

## Why

You asked for both. The favicon piece also explains the *"I don't see the new icon"* puzzle from the last message: `/favicon.svg` is what the browser tab renders, and that file was *still* the lightning-bolt glyph from before #137. The `/icon-N.png` set (which we did swap to EmDash) is only used for the iOS apple-touch-icon, the PWA install, and direct URL fetches like the LinkedIn submission upload.

## How — legal cleanup

- Privacy §10 contact: `oznakash@gmail.com` → `learnai@useyl.com`; drop the "Operator: Oz Akan…" line. GitHub-issues link stays (it's the project repo, not personal).
- Terms §14 contact: same.
- Terms §12 (Governing law): no longer cross-references the operator by name. Rephrased to *"the law applicable where the Service is operated."* The EU/EEA consumer-rights carve-out is preserved and slightly strengthened: *"and you keep the right to bring a claim in your country of residence."*

## How — favicon swap

`app/public/favicon.svg` is now the same content as `app/public/icon.svg` (EmDash on the brand-gradient square). One source of truth across:

- Browser tab favicon (this PR)
- iOS apple-touch-icon (already done in #137)
- PWA manifest sizes (already done)
- LinkedIn submission upload at `/icon-400.png` (already done)

Browsers cache favicons aggressively (the response sets `immutable`), so **existing visitors need a hard refresh (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R)** to see the change in their tab. New visitors and any external sharing surface (LinkedIn submission preview, Slack/Twitter unfurls, direct `/icon-400.png` fetches) get the new mark immediately.

## Test plan

- [ ] Once deployed, `https://learnai.cloud-claude.com/privacy` no longer contains `oznakash@gmail.com` or `Oz Akan`.
- [ ] `/terms` same check.
- [ ] Both pages show `learnai@useyl.com` in the contact section.
- [ ] After a hard refresh, the browser tab shows the EmDash favicon.
- [ ] `/favicon.svg` byte-equals `/icon.svg`.

author: sonichi
body:
## Summary

Folds the never-shipped `/personal-reactive-loop` sub-loop draft into Sutando.app's existing polling-timer infrastructure. Chip refresh has no LLM round-trip — `gh pr list`, first `## Title` of `pending-questions.md`, recent results dir scan — so the natural home is the menu-bar app that already does watcher liveness on a 30s timer.

Per Chi's review 2026-05-05: *"if it's only scripts, can it be merged with the sutando app? The app also ensures watcher alive."*

## What lands

- **120s `Timer` in `applicationDidFinishLaunching`** → `refreshContextualChips()`. One-shot fires at startup so chips aren't stale-from-yesterday.
- **`refreshContextualChips()`** writes 3 chip types into `contextual-chips.json`:
  1. Open PRs authored by sonichi (top 3, via `gh pr list --repo sonichi/sutando --json number,title`)
  2. Top pending question (first `## Title` line of `pending-questions.md`)
  3. Most recent unread result (newest `results/task-*.txt` mtime, only if < 10min old)
- **Atomic write**: tmp + `FileManager.replaceItemAt`. Cleanup on rename failure.
- **`runShell()` helper** with two corrections vs naive Process invocation:
  1. Explicit PATH including `/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin` — apps launched via `open` get a minimal PATH that excludes Homebrew paths. Without this, `gh` couldn't find `git`.
  2. Drains both stdout AND stderr pipes (avoids SIGPIPE on long stderr).
- **`gh` path resolution**: tries `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh` first, falls back to `/usr/local/bin/gh` (Intel). Avoids hardcoding for both Apple-Silicon and Intel layouts.
- **`gh --repo sonichi/sutando`**: the app's CWD when launched via `open` is the user's home dir, not a git repo. Without `--repo`, `gh` fails with `fatal: not a git repository`.

## Verified end-to-end

- swiftc -O clean compile
- App rebuilt + relaunched (`open src/Sutando/Sutando` per `feedback_sutando_app_launch_method.md`)
- `contextual-chips.json` written within seconds of startup with 3 PR-review chips + 1 pending-question chip
- 120s timer fires correctly; chips refresh without action

## Why this isn't a Claude Code skill

The decomposition discussion in this PR's prep landed on: **mechanical polling lives in the menu-bar Swift app, LLM-required reasoning stays as Claude Code skills.** The reactive-loop draft (private skill) had zero LLM calls — every step was a shell-out or file read. So the runtime cost of even firing a `/personal-reactive-loop` cron in Claude Code was wasted: prompt tokens for nothing the LLM has to decide.

The decomposition framing was right; the answer was "this concern lives in the app, not in a Claude Code skill." Future sub-loops that DO need LLM judgment (`/curate-loop` reasoning over `pending-questions.md`, `/build-loop` picking work) stay as Claude Code skills. This split frees the Claude Code session entirely for those.

## Companion change in private repo

Deletes `~/.sutando-memory-sync/skills/personal-reactive-loop/` (the draft this PR supersedes). Will be in next memory-sync push.

author: origamihase
body:
## Severity
MEDIUM — defense-in-depth gap in the local secret scanner. No secret is currently leaked; this hardens detection of a class of secrets that was previously partial-only.

## Vulnerability
SendGrid API keys use the structural format `SG.<22 chars>.<43 chars>` (~67 characters total, three segments separated by `.`).

The scanner's generic high-entropy fallback uses the character class `[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{24,}`, which **does not include `.`**. As a result the fallback could not match the full token across the dot-separated segments. In practice:

- In a sensitive assignment (e.g. `SENDGRID_API_KEY = "SG…"`), the generic assignment detector caught the value but reported it as the unspecific reason `"Verdächtige Zuweisung eines potentiellen Secrets"`.
- In a non-sensitive context (e.g. `connect("SG…")`), only the **trailing 43-character segment** was flagged. The `SG.` prefix and the 22-char identifier silently disappeared from the report, and the finding's reason was the generic `"Hochentropischer Token-String"` with no SendGrid attribution.

This means a developer or a CI run looking at the scan output had no signal that the leak was a SendGrid key, slowing down triage and revocation, and the finding was easier to dismiss as a generic high-entropy false positive.

## Impact
A leaked SendGrid API key generally grants the holder full ability to send email on behalf of the account (subject to scope), read mail logs, and in some cases manage account resources. Without specific attribution, an emergency response is slower because the responder has to identify the issuer from the redacted snippet (`SG.A***h345` after redaction) before they know which dashboard to revoke from.

## Fix
Adds one entry to `_KNOWN_TOKENS` in `src/utils/secret_scanner.py`:

```python
(re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])SG\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{22}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{43}(?![A-Za-z0-9])"),
 "SendGrid API Key gefunden"),
```

This is consistent with how Anthropic, OpenAI and the GitHub `gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_` patterns were added in earlier sentinel passes — a strict regex with explicit lookarounds and an issuer-named reason. The pattern is unambiguous because no other documented credential format starts with `SG.`, so false-positive risk is negligible.

## Verification
- New test file `tests/test_secret_scanner_sendgrid.py` covers:
  - detection in a sensitive variable assignment,
  - detection in a function-call context (the gap that previously dropped the prefix), and
  - correct redaction of the displayed `match` (first 4 + `***` + last 4 for a 67-char token).
- All 54 secret-scanner tests pass: `pytest tests/test_secret_scanner*.py` → 54 passed.
- Wider security suite passes: `pytest tests/test_secret_scanner*.py tests/test_log_sanitization*.py tests/test_logging_sanitize.py` → 166 passed.
- `ruff check` clean on both touched files.
- `mypy` shows no new errors on `src/utils/secret_scanner.py` (the 8 pre-existing errors in `src/utils/http.py` are unchanged from `main`).
- Repo-wide self-scan passes: `python3 scripts/scan_secrets.py` → "Keine potentiellen Secrets gefunden."

## Notes for reviewer
Change is +10 lines of production code (one regex entry + a 4-line comment explaining the entropy-fallback gap) plus a self-contained test module. Journal entry added under `.jules/sentinel.md` documenting the multi-segment-token blind spot for future passes.

author: vandranki
body:
## Summary

`/v1/messages/count_tokens` against a Vertex AI partner model (e.g. `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6`) returned `input_tokens` that ignored the `system` prompt entirely. The same request against `azure_ai/` and `bedrock/` Claude correctly accounted for the system prompt.

## Root cause

The `system` parameter was received by `VertexAITokenCounter.count_tokens` (`litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py`) but was never forwarded downstream:

1. `common_utils.py:1142` — `partner_models_handler.count_tokens()` was called without the `system` argument even though it was available in scope.
2. `vertex_ai_partner_models/main.py:317` — `VertexAIPartnerModels.count_tokens` built `request_data = {"model": model, "messages": messages}` without a `system` key, so even if the caller had passed it, it would have been dropped before reaching the Anthropic count-tokens endpoint on Vertex AI.

`VertexAIPartnerModelsTokenCounter.handle_count_tokens_request` posts `request_data` directly to the Vertex AI endpoint, which accepts and correctly counts `system` tokens when the field is present.

## Fix

**`common_utils.py`** — pass `system=system` when calling `partner_models_handler.count_tokens()`.

**`vertex_ai_partner_models/main.py`** — add `system=None` to the `count_tokens` signature and include `request_data["system"] = system` when `system` is not `None`.

No changes needed in `handler.py` — it already passes `request_data` through as-is.

Fixes #27113

## Summary

The "Derive registry trigger inputs" step in
`publish-docs-to-s3.yml` runs
`python3 dev/registry/derive_wave_providers.py` unconditionally in
the Build Info job. The downstream `update-registry` job only runs
when `registry-providers != ''` or `registry-full-build == 'true'` —
so for non-provider distributions (`apache-airflow`,
`apache-airflow-ctl`, `apache-airflow-task-sdk`, `helm-chart`,
`docker-stack`) the script's output isn't consumed and the script
invocation is a no-op.

This PR skips the script invocation for those distributions:

- Both `registry-providers=` and `registry-full-build=false` are
  set so the `update-registry` job skips downstream as expected.
- Release tags cut before #66100 (when the script was added) can
  publish docs again without the workflow tripping on the missing
  file. Surfaced while publishing docs for `airflow-ctl/0.1.4`
  (cut from `0.1.4rc3` on 2026-04-22).

The non-provider list is kept in sync with `NON_PROVIDER_TOKENS` in

author: lngdao
body:
## Summary

Live observation 2026-05-06 01:19 — \`execute_order\` on XAUUSD sized **0.67 lot** at 0.5% risk on \$1874 equity. Realized risk at SL would have been **\$938 (~50% of equity)** — 100x over the 0.5% intended budget. Anh's analysis (verbatim screenshot):

> Risk engine dùng: 1 lot × \$1 giá. Thực tế XAUUSD: \$100/lot.
> Nó sai contract size — thiếu factor 100.

Confirmed in \`crates/kairos/src/handlers/mod.rs:695\`:

\`\`\`rust
let total_quantity = risk_amount / stop_distance;
//                                              ↑ MISSING × contract_size
\`\`\`

Forex-pair-only assumption. Wrong for XAUUSD, XAGUSD, and any instrument where 1 lot ≠ 1 USD-equivalent unit.

## Fix

New module \`crate::risk::asset_specs\` ships:

| Symbol | contract_size | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| XAUUSD | 100 | 100 oz per lot, price USD/oz |
| XAGUSD | 5000 | silver standard |
| EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY | 100,000 | forex standard lot |
| BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/SOLUSDT | 1.0 | crypto spot direct quantity |
| Pattern: \`<MAJOR><MAJOR>\` | 100,000 | unlisted forex pairs (EURJPY, AUDCAD…) |
| Pattern: \`*USDT/USDC/BUSD\` | 1.0 | unlisted crypto pairs |
| Unknown | 1.0 + warn | logs to operator for table coverage |

Sizing now: \`risk_amount / (stop_distance × contract_size)\`.

For XAUUSD anh's setup (\$1874 equity, 0.5% risk, 14 USD SL):
- **before**: 0.67 lot (100x over-leveraged)
- **after**: 0.0067 lot — below MT5 min lot 0.01, fails fast pre-submit via volume_step rounding (PR #79)

→ Anh needs higher equity OR wider risk_pct OR tighter stop để trade XAU. With a paper test: \$10k equity + 0.5% risk + 14 USD SL = \$50 / 1400 = 0.0357 lot → rounds to 0.03 lot. OK.

## Coverage

10 unit tests in \`asset_specs::tests\`:
- contract_size correctness per symbol (XAUUSD=100, EURUSD=100k, BTCUSDT=1)
- case-insensitive lookup
- forex pattern fallback (EURJPY, AUDCAD, NZDCHF)
- crypto pattern fallback (ADAUSDT, DOGEUSDT)
- unknown symbol → default
- **\`xauusd_sizing_math_matches_live_observation\`** — reproduces 0.67 lot bug without contract_size, 0.0067 lot fixed, exact 100x ratio

\`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings\` clean. Existing 2200+ tests unaffected.

## Future improvement (NOT in this PR)

Hardcoded table covers anh's instrument universe. For broader broker support, query \`SymbolInfoDouble(symbol, SYMBOL_TRADE_CONTRACT_SIZE)\` from MT5 EA at boot per symbol; cache. Same EA-symbol-info pull also subsumes \`SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP\` from PR #79. Single future PR can replace both hardcoded tables with EA-queried metadata.

## Companion PRs

- **#77** — full sibling t1 error logged in kairos.log
- **#78** — execute_order chat-driven direct execution tool
- **#79** — MT5 volume_step rounding (broker-acceptable lot, all 4 EA transports)

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test -p risk asset_specs\` — 10/10 pass
- [x] \`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings\` clean
- [ ] Anh rebuild + relaunch — re-test execute_order trên XAUUSD with proper equity. Should reject sub-min-lot (PR #79) instead of sizing 0.67 lot.

Closes #1270

## Summary

`vibewarden.reference.yaml` claims to document EVERY supported option but was missing 13 fields that exist in `internal/config` Go structs. This PR fills the gap.

**Sections added:**

- `resilience` — upstream timeout, circuit breaker, and retry configuration (default: timeout 30s, CB/retry disabled)
- `webhooks` — outbound event delivery endpoints + inbound HMAC signature verification
- `overrides` — escape hatches for hand-crafted kratos.yml, docker-compose.yml, and identity schema
- `observability` — local Grafana/Prometheus/Loki stack under the "observability" Compose profile
- `audit` — security audit log sink (enabled by default, writes to stdout)
- `input_validation` — URL/query-string/header size limits (default: disabled)
- `error_pages` — custom HTML/JSON error bodies by status code (default: disabled)
- `maintenance` — 503 maintenance mode (default: disabled)
- `compression` — response compression algorithms (default: enabled, zstd/gzip)
- `response_headers` — arbitrary set/add/remove of response headers
- `watch` — config file watcher for hot reload (default: enabled, 500ms debounce)
- `tls.cert_monitoring` — certificate expiry monitor sub-section (nested under existing `tls:`)
- `log.access_log` — access log toggle (nested under existing `log:`)

**New test:** `internal/config/reference_yaml_test.go` — uses `LoadRaw` to parse the reference YAML into `Config` and asserts sentinel values for all 13 added fields plus core existing fields. Catches malformed YAML and mapstructure tag mismatches.

**Note on `deploy`:** The issue listed `deploy` as a candidate but it was added by #1320 (already merged). Verified present before writing.

author: creaactivai
body:
## Summary

Three targeted fixes for the highest-severity student-reported bugs from the platform audit:

- **CRITICAL #1** — Quiz submission no longer crashes when a quiz has 0 questions ([server/routes.ts:3781-3783](https://github.com/creaactivai/Cogniboost/blob/claude/gracious-ishizaka-c9d1b6/server/routes.ts#L3781-L3783)). Previously `correctCount / questions.length` produced `NaN`, which the integer `score` column rejected, wedging the attempt and blocking retry.
- **CRITICAL #2** — AI quiz generation (both the module-video endpoint and the lesson-quiz endpoint) now validates the parsed JSON: rejects empty arrays, drops malformed questions (`options.length !== 4`, `correctOptionIndex` out of `[0,3]`, empty strings), and surfaces the **real** OpenAI / parsing error to admins instead of the opaque generic "Failed to generate quiz" 500. This eliminates the silent path where a successful 200 returned 0 questions and then triggered #1 on the student side.
- **HIGH #6** — On video-quiz pass, the client now calls `refetchProgress()` in addition to invalidating the modules query ([client/src/components/dashboard/course-viewer.tsx:183](https://github.com/creaactivai/Cogniboost/blob/claude/gracious-ishizaka-c9d1b6/client/src/components/dashboard/course-viewer.tsx#L183)). Previously the next lesson stayed locked in the UI until manual refresh, even though the backend had unlocked it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual: open a quiz that has had its questions deleted in admin → submit → expect 400 "Quiz has no questions yet" instead of 500/wedged attempt.
- [ ] Manual: trigger AI generation on a module with a transcript that's likely to confuse the model (e.g. very short or empty) → expect a specific error string in the admin toast, not "Failed to generate video quiz."
- [ ] Manual: pass a video quiz → next lesson card should immediately become unlockable without page refresh.
- [ ] Confirm `npm run check` passes on CI.
- [ ] Confirm Railway deploy comes up cleanly.

## Notes

- No schema migrations.
- No new env vars.
- Behavior on the happy path (quiz with valid questions, AI returning a normal response) is unchanged.
- Source of the audit and ranking: [internal platform audit thread, this branch].

- `packages/vinext/src/server/app-route-handler-policy.ts` — `resolveAppRouteHandlerSpecialError` now uses the shared parsers.

## Preserved per-call-site behaviour

The shared parsers return only the raw shape (`{ type, url, status }` for redirects, `{ status }` for HTTP error fallbacks). Each caller still owns its own post-processing:

- `app-server-action-execution.ts` keeps the `Number.isInteger(statusCode)` guard for HTTP error digests in `getActionControlResponse`.
- `app-server-action-execution.ts` `getActionRedirect` keeps the full `{ status, type, url }` shape (only this site uses the redirect `type`).
- `app-route-handler-policy.ts` keeps `new URL(redirectUrl, requestUrl).toString()` resolution and the `isAction ? 303 : redirect.status` override.
- `app-page-execution.ts` keeps the basePath-and-cookie merging at the call site.

## Minor unification

`parseNextRedirectDigest` returns `null` when the encoded URL segment is missing — matching the existing guard in `app-server-action-execution.ts`. The page and route-handler call sites previously would have thrown `URIError` from `decodeURIComponent(undefined)` for a malformed `NEXT_REDIRECT;` digest with no URL; they now treat it as not-a-redirect and let the error propagate. This case is unreachable for any digest Next.js actually emits.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vp test run tests/app-router.test.ts` — 308 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm fmt --write` on touched files — clean
- [x] `pnpm knip` — clean
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` on the vinext package — clean

body: Description ----------------------------------------------------- This PR adds the new Environment Stratification tool to Breedbase. The tool allows users to select a dataset and trait, run environment stratification analysis, and review compatible environment groups based on genotype-by- environment interaction. Results are returned through a new AJAX controller, processed by an R backend script, and displayed in a dedicated Mason/JavaScript interface. Main Features - New Environment Stratification page and UI. - Dataset and trait selection using existing Breedbase dataset tools. - R-based environment stratification analysis. - Pairwise environment compatibility testing. - Group summary output for statistically compatible environments. - ANOVA output tab with automatic experimental design detection. - Ungrouped environment output. - Interactive map showing trial locations and environment groups. - Hover tooltips on map markers showing location and trial name. - XLSX downloads for result tables. ANOVA / Design Handling The R script detects the available experimental design information and builds the ANOVA model accordingly. Supported fixed-effect ANOVA structures include: - CRD - RCBD - Incomplete block / alpha-lattice - Augmented / block-only - Row-column / augmented row-column Row and column terms are only used when the trial design is explicitly row-column/spatial. They are ignored for CRD and RCBD even if coordinate columns are present. author: jeliason
body:
Three issues observed in Logfire traces of pdac-build cytokine extraction (gpt-5.5):

1. **FigureExcerpt subschema undocumented.** Agent emitted floats for figure_excerpt.value (str field), invented forbidden fields (panel, group, caption_excerpt), omitted required figure_id. One IL-10 retry racked up 80 validation errors.
2. **TableExcerpt subschema not documented at all.**
3. **experimental_denominator was labeled optional** but validator requires it for density/per-mass observables (units like pg/mg with support=positive).

This PR adds explicit YAML schemas for both excerpt types (all-string, extra=forbid), flags the common invented-field mistakes, clarifies that figure_excerpt.value is a text annotation of what was read (not the digitized numeric value), and updates experimental_denominator from optional → conditionally required with the exact validator error message inline.

author: samn
body:
The operator-socket tests in server.test.ts hardcoded `agent_uid: 0` because
UID 0 (root) reliably has its own primary group and is not a member of regular
users' groups, satisfying the operator-socket trust-boundary check
(`agent_uid !== gate uid`). When the test process itself runs as root,
`gate uid` is also 0, so `startGateServer` aborts with "agent_uid (0) equals
gate uid" before the assertion under test can fire — six operator-socket tests
fail spuriously.

Switch the agent UID to `nobody` (65534) when the gate UID is 0, keeping the
existing UID 0 selection for non-root runs. `nobody` has its own primary
group and is universally not in `root`, so it satisfies both the
trust-boundary and operator-group-membership guardrails.

author: pipex
body:
Implement update lock management for host apps.

An app is locked before any stop operations take place and the service tries to take all locks held by the services. For running containers, it uses the corresponding host path to the `/tmp/balena` mount, ensuring that even if changing the host path, old locks will still be respected.

The main differences with respect to the existing supervisor lock management are 
- We no longer check `resin-updates.lock`, this is a legacy path that should not be used anymore
- All service containers share the same lock path, effectively having one lock per application. This is probably how it should have always been once we moved to multi-container

Depends-on: #112

author: cristian-pisco
body:
## Problem

The team's standing rule is *E2E required for any frontend change, regardless of MVP status*, but the spec → proposal → QA pipeline lets that rule be punted. Spec authors write "E2E not required for MVP", proposal agents echo it, and `/jlu:ui-qa-run` exits cleanly when no `user-flow.md` exists — so UI changes ship without browser-level coverage.

## Impact

- **Spec gate** — `jlu-spec-interviewer` rejects the three known deferral phrasings ("not required for MVP", "manual QA covers it", "defer to follow-up") and requires at least one Success Criterion describing a browser-level flow when a UI service is in scope.
- **Proposal gate** — `jlu-proposal-agent` forbids the same phrasings in `PROPOSAL.md`. Testing Strategy must list E2E flows traced to SCs and the phase plan must include a `/jlu:ui-qa-run` run.
- **QA workflow** — `ui-qa-run.md`:
  - Hardens UI-service detection (stack field OR description regex), so legacy registrations without a `stack` field still trigger E2E.
  - Refuses to exit-0 when a UI service is missing a `dev` block — it's now a hard error with remediation hint.
  - Dispatches `jlu-ui-e2e-writer` in `MODE=derive-from-spec` when no `user-flow.md` exists, generates one from `SPEC.md` (Routes, Steps, Boot Order, Env Vars, Auth Precondition), and commits it back to the task directory.
- **E2E writer** — `jlu-ui-e2e-writer` gains a `derive-from-spec` mode with explicit derivation rules and `NEEDS_CONTEXT` escalations for ambiguous inputs (missing route hint, unclassified boot order, missing auth role).

`.opencode/agents/` mirrors regenerated. `npm test` (339/339) and `node bin/sync-agents.mjs --check` pass locally.

author: asenlog
body:
## Summary

When the plugin runs inside an Orthanc process, every `ReceiveMessage` fails immediately with `curlCode: 27, Out of memory`. The error is real but misleading — it isn't OOM, and it isn't a libcurl init-flag issue.

**Root cause:** `Aws::InitAPI` always pulls in `aws-c-io`, which calls `s2n_init()`. On every OpenSSL 3.x we tested (Ubuntu 25.10 / 24.04, Debian Bookworm), `s2n_init` mutates global OpenSSL state in a way that makes `SSL_CTX_new(TLS_client_method())` return `NULL` for the rest of the process's life. libcurl needs that call for every HTTPS request, so its TLS setup fails — and libcurl reports the failure as `CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY (27)`.

**Fix:** build the AWS SDK with `-DUSE_CRT_HTTP_CLIENT=ON` so it uses the AWS CRT HTTP client (which goes through s2n natively) instead of `CurlHttpClient`. libcurl is no longer in the SDK's HTTP path, so the corrupted libcurl/OpenSSL state never matters. One-line build-flag change, no plugin source changes.

## Diagnosis

Full investigation in `docs/curl-error-27-investigation.md`, including:

- two wrong paths I went down first (`httpOptions.initAndCleanupCurl=false`; disabling the Python plugin), and the trace-log line that re-pointed to s2n
- a minimal `SSL_CTX_new` before/after `Aws::InitAPI` probe (the conclusive test)
- a further-narrowed test that `dlopen`s `libs2n.so` and calls only `s2n_init` — no AWS SDK at all — and reproduces the same OpenSSL breakage in two lines of output
- every hypothesis ruled out, with the exact test that ruled it out
- the validation that `USE_CRT_HTTP_CLIENT=ON` removes libcurl from the SDK's `NEEDED` entries
- known caveat: this only matters if the host process needs libcurl HTTPS for something else; in our typical Orthanc deployments it doesn't

## Test plan

- [x] Build SDK with the flag — succeeds
- [x] Verify `libaws-cpp-sdk-core.so` no longer links to libcurl (`objdump -p | grep NEEDED`) — confirmed
- [x] Deploy into a running orthanc container; confirm the libcurl/OpenSSL `curlCode 27` error is gone
- [ ] Confirm successful SQS receive on a host with working RDRAND (local test machine has the AMD Picasso RDRAND-disabled microcode bug, which now exposes a separate s2n RNG failure on this CPU only — does not affect production hardware)

## Summary

Lays the foundation for issue #430 by reorganising the settings tab into collapsible sections, replacing the previous flat scroll with a scannable list of section headings. Implements the `<details>`-based approach from the issue plan; modal extractions for Tool Permissions, MCP Servers, and Vault Search are intentionally deferred to follow-up PRs.

Fixes #430 (foundation — modal-extraction follow-ups tracked separately).

## Changes

- New `createCollapsibleSection(plugin, containerEl, title, id)` helper in `src/ui/settings-helpers.ts` that renders a styled `<details>` and returns the inner content element. Uses plain DOM APIs (not Obsidian's `createEl` extensions) so it works in jsdom-based unit tests with stub containers.
- New `expandedSettingsSections: string[]` setting (default `[]`) persists which sections are open across plugin reloads.
- Converted all 13 existing `.setHeading()` calls to collapsibles: General (new wrapper for previously un-headed top of `settings-general.ts`), Scheduled Tasks, Lifecycle Hooks, Session History, UI Settings, Context Management, Custom Prompts, API Configuration, Tool Execution, Tool Permissions, Tool Loop Detection, MCP Servers, Vault Search Index. The existing **Show Advanced Settings** toggle still gates the seven advanced sections.
- Bug fix: Provider change in the General section now re-renders only that section's content via a new `renderGeneralSection` inner function, instead of `containerEl.empty()` + re-rendering only General — which previously tore down later-rendered sections (UI / Context / Advanced) on the outer container.
- CSS for the section styling: native `<details>` with a custom rotating chevron, hover states matching `var(--text-accent)`, top borders to delineate sections.
- Docs: `docs/reference/settings.md` updated with an intro paragraph describing the new layout and a `expandedSettingsSections` reference entry listing all known section ids.

author: pberton
body:
## Summary

Support `cache_from` and `cache_to` fields in the compose file's `build` section, passing them as `--cache-from` and `--cache-to` flags to the `docker buildx build` command. This enables GitHub Actions cache (`type=gha`) and other Docker BuildKit cache backends when using `build-from-repo`.

### Example compose config:
```yaml
services:
  web:
    build:
      context: .
      cache_from:
        - type=gha
      cache_to:
        - type=gha,mode=max
```

## Changes

- **`cmd/build/build_from_repo.go`**: Extract `CacheFrom`/`CacheTo` per service from compose-go parsed project and pass to docker build
- **`cmd/build/utils.go`**: Add `BuildDockerBuildArgs()` helper for testable arg construction; skip `--load` when `--cache-to` is set or when building for multiple platforms (incompatible with `docker buildx --load`)
- **`cmd/build/utils_test.go`**: Unit tests for arg construction (6 cases including multi-platform) and compose cache parsing
- **`test/smoke_test/build/dockercache/`**: E2E smoke test with full `build-from-repo --dry-run` using GHA cache
- **`.github/workflows/smoke-tests.yml`**: Dedicated `smoke-tests-docker-cache` job with Docker Buildx setup

## Key behavior

- `--load` is skipped when `--cache-to` is set (build purpose is cache population)
- `--load` is skipped when multiple platforms are specified (e.g., `linux/amd64,linux/arm64`) since Docker cannot load multi-arch images into the local daemon

body:
## Plan citation

`phase-1-minimal-secure-messaging.md` §5 Track D **D1** — "Trace Checkpoint Expansion. Add discovery and capability checkpoints. Include decision reason codes and artifact versions." Closes:

- the **capability checkpoint** (discovery checkpoint stays open until Track A),
- the **decision reason codes** sub-bullet (`reason_code` shipped in the previous PR; this PR confirms it appears on every event),
- the **artifact versions** sub-bullet (new field).

Also tightens the **emission topology** for the audit event schema contract.

## Summary

`verify_envelope` now emits a separate `capability.verify` `AuditEvent` in addition to the existing `envelope.verify`. Emission topology:

| Outcome | Events emitted (in order) |
|---|---|
| Success | `capability.verify` allow → `envelope.verify` allow |
| Pre-cap deny (digest mismatch, expired envelope, etc.) | `envelope.verify` deny only |
| Cap-level deny (revoked, sub mismatch, etc.) | `capability.verify` deny → `envelope.verify` deny (same `reason_code`) |
| Post-cap deny (replay) | `capability.verify` allow → `envelope.verify` deny (`replay_detected`) |

`AuditEvent` grows `artifact_version` (defaulted, appended last to `_HASHED_FIELDS` so existing chains stay valid per the extension convention). v0 emits `"envelope/v0"` for envelope checkpoints and `"wt-cap+jwt"` for capability checkpoints. `JsonlAuditSink.read_all` defaults the field to `""` when reading legacy lines.

## Schema contract update

`audit-event-schema.md` gains the **Emission topology** table and the `artifact_version` row. The existing test vector `audit-event.jsonl` is regenerated to demonstrate all three scenarios across five events.

author: davidalee
body:
## Summary

`ce-code-review` is a skill, but its branch-mode and standalone-mode bash blocks invoked the merge-base helper as `bash scripts/resolve-base.sh`. The Bash tool runs from the user's project CWD — not the skill directory — so that path resolves against the **reviewed repo**, not the bundled skill. Two concrete failure modes:

1. **Correctness (loud-fail):** in any reviewed repo without a `scripts/resolve-base.sh`, bash exits non-zero, the existing `||` branch prints `ERROR: resolve-base.sh failed`, and the skill aborts. Branch and standalone modes are effectively unusable on the common case — users have to fall back to `base:<ref>` or PR mode.
2. **Security (silent-corruption):** if the reviewed repo *does* ship its own `scripts/resolve-base.sh`, the reviewer executes that repo-controlled script with no error and computes a plausible-looking but completely attacker-controlled merge-base. Low-likelihood, high-impact for a tool whose job is summarizing untrusted code.

This PR resolves the helper from `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` instead, with an in-CWD-rejection check and an explicit fail-closed branch when the variable is unavailable or hostile.

## Why this went unnoticed

- **PR mode dominates real usage.** `/ce-code-review <NNN>` resolves the base from `gh pr view` and never touches `resolve-base.sh`, so most invocations don't hit the broken path.
- **The error read like a config problem.** `ERROR: resolve-base.sh failed` looks like "set up your repo" rather than "the skill is misrouting." Users likely worked around it with `base:<ref>` and moved on.
- **The contract test only matched output strings**, not that the path resolves through the harness rather than the CWD — so CI was happy. The updated test in this PR pins the probe shape and forbids the bare relative-path form.

## What changed

- Branch and standalone modes now resolve `resolve-base.sh` from `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/resolve-base.sh`. AGENTS.md documents `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` as the canonical primitive for skill-bundled scripts and asserts it resolves correctly across `claude --plugin-dir` and standard marketplace-cached installs.
- The candidate is `realpath`'d and rejected if it resolves to the reviewed repo's CWD or any path inside it — so even a misconfigured or hostile harness that points `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` at a directory inside the reviewed repo cannot be used to execute a repo-controlled script.
- If the variable is unexposed or resolves inside the reviewed repo, the skill prints a precise error and stops, telling the user to re-run with `base:<ref>` or use a harness that exposes the skill directory.
- The pre-existing fail-closed posture is preserved: under any failure (missing variable, missing script, script-emitted `ERROR:`), the reviewer refuses to fall back to `git diff HEAD`, which would only show uncommitted changes and silently miss every committed change on the branch.
- **No bare relative-path fallback.** Adding `scripts/resolve-base.sh` as a last-resort would re-introduce the original CWD-resolution bug *and* the script-shadowing security path, so the contract test now asserts that fallback is absent (`expect(content).not.toMatch(/bash\s+scripts\/resolve-base\.sh/)`).

## Cross-platform behavior

This skill is converted for non-Claude targets (Codex, Cursor, Gemini, etc.) and the `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` variable remains literal in the converted output. On those platforms the probe finds no script and the skill fails closed with a clear instruction to pass `base:<ref>` — strictly safer than executing a CWD-relative script. PR mode (`<NNN>`) is unaffected and continues to resolve the base from PR metadata via `gh`.

## Empirical evidence

Reproduced in a throwaway repo with a decoy `scripts/resolve-base.sh` that prints `BASE:DECOYWASEXECUTED` and exits 0 — i.e., a worst-case reviewed repo carrying its own helper at the path the old code probed. Same CWD, same decoy, both invocations:

```
== OLD (bash scripts/resolve-base.sh) ==
$ bash scripts/resolve-base.sh
BASE:DECOYWASEXECUTED
exit=0

== NEW (probe block, with CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR set) ==
$ # probe resolves RESOLVE_SCRIPT to the bundled helper, ignores the decoy
exit=0
BASE=a9bafc43416f078e9841994b6112509d5049266b   # real merge-base from the bundled helper
```

The OLD path silently executed the reviewed repo's script and returned its forged base. The NEW path resolved through `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, ignored the decoy, and returned the real `git merge-base` sha. The loud-fail case (no decoy present in the reviewed repo) produces `bash: scripts/resolve-base.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) under OLD and the documented fail-closed error under NEW with no harness variable set.

## Verification

- `bun test tests/review-skill-contract.test.ts` — 26 pass, including the updated `fails closed when merge-base is unresolved` contract (pins the new probe shape, asserts absence of the relative-path fallback) and a new `resolve-base probe resolves CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR and rejects repo-controlled paths` test that exercises the probe end-to-end against synthetic harnesses (unset, empty, happy-path with CWD decoy present, and hostile harness pointing into the reviewed-repo CWD).
- `bun test` — full suite (1240 tests) passes.
- `bun run release:validate` — clean.

## Test plan

- [x] Branch mode on a feature branch with `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` set: helper resolves, diff is correct against merge-base.
- [x] Standalone mode on the current branch: same as above.
- [x] Reviewed repo containing a decoy `scripts/resolve-base.sh`: decoy is **not** executed; bundled helper runs.
- [x] Hostile harness with `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` pointing inside the reviewed repo: rejected, fail-closed; decoy not executed.
- [x] Harness with no `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` exposed: skill prints the documented error and stops; no `git diff HEAD` fallback.
- [x] PR mode (`<NNN>`): unchanged — still resolves base from PR metadata.

## Summary

- Replaces `make_parallel_wrapper` with `build_parallel_stages`, which materialises each parallel YAML block into three runtime stages: `<group>-fanout`, `<group>`, and `<group>-fanin`
- Fixes lost-bail race: `patch_state` now holds an exclusive `fcntl.flock` during every read-modify-write, and child bails go into `parallel_bails[child_key]` rather than the shared top-level slot
- Fixes bail cross-contamination: `check_bail` accepts an optional `child_key` and reads only that child's shard, so a sibling's bail is invisible to other children
- Adds `cancel_on_bail` and `bail_policy` (any|all) per-block YAML knobs; `StageContext` gains `child_key` and `worktree` fields
- Fan-in raises `NotImplementedError` for mutating worktrees (deferred until a concrete use case)

- Provide a minimal local MVP of an AI-powered Discovery Agent that can be run on Windows for quick demos and iteration with a deterministic mock LLM backend. 
- Enable generation and validation flows for discovery artifacts using replaceable agent/LLM abstractions so a corporate LLM client can be integrated later.

💡 **What:** Replaced the sequential `for (const c of checks)` loop around line 15447 in `modules/route-assistant/panel.js` with `await Promise.all(checks.map(async ...))` for concurrently saving calibration overrides. 

🎯 **Why:** `await` inside a loop forces a wait for each storage operation to finish before moving to the next route in the batch. Parallelizing this removes the bottleneck and speeds up overall time taken proportional to the number of records selected.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** In a local benchmark simulating sequential vs parallel save delays over 50 records with a conservative 5ms latency, the total execution time dropped from 271.55ms to 5.65ms (a roughly ~48x improvement). Real-world performance using `chrome.storage.local` with concurrent sets will observe a substantial snappiness during batch application.

## Summary
- On HA restart, the cover platform sometimes registers entities late (Homematic IP is the report in #342). The integration's first refresh would call `set_cover_position` before the entity existed, producing a "missing or not currently available" warning and — on platforms that queue commands — replaying the wrong target once the entity came online, moving the cover.

body:
## Summary

- Adds three hardening scalars to `vsphere.host` so audits can assert on host posture without traversing the `properties` dict:
  - `lockdownMode string` — `HostSystem.Config.LockdownMode` (`lockdownDisabled` / `lockdownNormal` / `lockdownStrict`).
  - `firewallEnabled bool` — `HostSystem.Config.Firewall.DefaultPolicy.IncomingBlocked`. The host firewall service itself is always running on ESXi; this field reflects default-deny posture, which is the CIS-relevant signal.
  - `secureBootEnabled bool` — `HostSystem.Capability.UefiSecureBoot` (vSphere 8.0.3+; older hosts report `false`).
- Reworks the misleading error that fired when calling `vsphere.host` (singular) on a vCenter connection. The old message claimed an "esxi resource" couldn't be resolved; the new one names the actual resource and points users at `vsphere.datacenter.hosts` / `vsphere.cluster.hosts`.

Both creation paths (`initVsphereHost` and `newVsphereHostResources`) populate the new fields via a small `hostHardeningArgs` helper that nil-guards `Config`, `Firewall`, and `Capability`.

New `.lr.versions` entries are at `13.0.10`.

## Test plan

| License       | MIT

When a platform call throws (rate limit, network error, etc.), the bundle's DataCollector re-runs the conversion during `kernel.response` to build profile data, so it throws the exception again. From the user's perspective, their `try/catch` around the agent looks broken: a 429 turns into a 500.

  Fix:

  - `DataCollector::awaitCallResults()` — wrap the per-call work in try/catch. Failed calls are recorded as result_type: 'error' with an error array (class, message), and the profiler template renders them. 
  - `DeferredResult::getResult()` — cache the exception; re-throw the same instance on subsequent calls. 

This bug only affects the development environment because the data collector only runs with `kernel.debug=true`.

BTW, Claude helped me debug the issue and find a proper solution

author: snodgrass-wilkerschnoz
body:
## Summary

Adds a priority parameter to platform adapters allowing messages to be sent silently (no notification buzz) or with normal/urgent notification levels.

## Changes

### Platform Adapters
- **base.py**: Add `priority: Literal["silent", "normal", "urgent"]` to abstract `send()` method
- **telegram.py**: Implement priority using `disable_notification` Telegram API parameter
- **discord.py**: Implement priority using `MessageFlags(4096)` for silent messages

### Automatic Classification (stream_consumer.py)
- Add `_classify_priority()` function that analyzes message content and context
- **Silent** (no buzz): Progress updates, "still working", iterations, tool progress, segment breaks
- **Normal** (buzz): Final responses, completions, messages needing user attention
- **Urgent** (buzz): Errors, failures, authentication issues, blocked commands, approval requests

## Motivation

Users receive too many routine notifications (progress updates, iteration counts) when using Hermes in Telegram. This feature allows important messages to still buzz while routine messages arrive silently - all within the same conversation thread.

## Example Behavior

- "Still working on this..." → silent (no buzz)
- "Iteration 3/10..." → silent (no buzz)
- "Task completed!" → normal (buzz)
- "Error: API key invalid" → urgent (buzz)
- "Requires approval for this action" → urgent (buzz)

## Backward Compatibility

- Default priority is "normal" so existing behavior is unchanged
- Priority can be set via parameter or via `metadata["priority"]` for backward compat

### Prometheus Azure AD remote write OAuth client secret exposed via config API
[CVE-2026-42151](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42151) / [GHSA-wg65-39gg-5wfj](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-wg65-39gg-5wfj)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Users who use Azure AD remote write with OAuth authentication are impacted.

The `client_secret` field in the Azure AD remote write OAuth configuration (`storage/remote/azuread`) was typed as `string` instead of `Secret`. Prometheus redacts fields of type `Secret` when serving the configuration via the `/-/config` HTTP API endpoint. Because the field was a plain string, the Azure OAuth client secret was exposed in plaintext to any user or process with access to that endpoint.

##### Patches

The problem has been patched by changing `ClientSecret` in `OAuthConfig` to `Secret`. Users should upgrade to 3.11.3 or 3.5.3 LTS.

##### Workarounds

Users  who can not upgrade can switch to Managed Identity or Workload Identity authentication for Azure AD remote write, which do not involve a client secret.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`

### Prometheus: Remote read endpoint allows denial of service via crafted snappy payload
[CVE-2026-42154](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42154) / [GHSA-8rm2-7qqf-34qm](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-8rm2-7qqf-34qm)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

The remote read endpoint (`/api/v1/read`) does not validate the declared decoded length in a snappy-compressed request body before allocating memory.
An unauthenticated attacker can send a small payload that causes a huge heap allocation per request. Under concurrent load this can exhaust available memory and crash the Prometheus process.

##### Patches
_Has the problem been patched? What versions should users upgrade to?_

Fixed in 3.11.3 and 3.5.3 LTS. Users should upgrade to these versions or later.

##### Workarounds
User who can not upgrade can place Prometheus behind a reverse proxy or firewall that requires authentication before requests reach /api/v1/read.

### Prometheus vulnerable to stored XSS via crafted histogram bucket label values in the old web UI heatmap display
[GHSA-fw8g-cg8f-9j28](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw8g-cg8f-9j28)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

In the Prometheus server's legacy web UI (enabled via the command-line flag `--enable-feature=old-ui`), the histogram heatmap chart view does not escape `le` label values when inserting them into the HTML for use as axis tick mark labels.

An attacker who can inject crafted metrics (e.g. via a compromised scrape target, remote write, or OTLP receiver endpoint) can execute JavaScript in the browser of any Prometheus user who views the metric in the heatmap chart UI. From the XSS context, an attacker could for example:

- Read `/api/v1/status/config` to extract sensitive configuration (although credentials / secrets are redacted by the server)
- Call `/-/quit` to shut down Prometheus (only if `--web.enable-lifecycle` is set)
- Call `/api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series` to delete data (only if `--web.enable-admin-api` is set)
- Exfiltrate metric data to an external server

Note that this only affects users who have explicitly enabled the legacy Prometheus web UI using the `--enable-feature=old-ui` command-line flag.

##### Patches

A patch is available at https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/releases/tag/v0.311.3.

##### Workarounds

If at all possible, disable the legacy web UI by removing the `--enable-feature=old-ui` command-line flag).

If this is not an option, take the following precautions:

- If using the remote write receiver (`--web.enable-remote-write-receiver`), ensure it is not exposed to untrusted sources.
- If using the OTLP receiver (`--web.enable-otlp-receiver`), ensure it is not exposed to untrusted sources.
- Ensure scrape targets are trusted and not under attacker control.
- Do not enable admin / mutating API endpoints (e.g. `--web.enable-admin-api` or `web.enable-lifecycle`) in cases where you cannot prevent untrusted data from being ingested.
- Users should avoid clicking untrusted links, especially those containing functions such as `label_replace`, as they may generate poisoned label names and values.

##### Resources

- CVE-2019-10215 — prior stored DOM XSS vulnerability in Prometheus query history, fixed in v2.7.2
- CVE-2026-40179 — prior stored DOM XSS vulnerability in Prometheus web UI (hover tooltips and metrics explorer), fixed in v3.11.2

Medium

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1212810093780571/task/1214560893964014?focus=true 

### Description

#### Context

The DuckDuckGo input screen already shows URL autocomplete suggestions on the chat tab when the. The native input field only showed chat history. This PR brings the same chat-tab URL suggestions experience to the native input field.

The work is split into two commits:

1. **Extract settings and flows from chat suggestion reader**: moves shared utilities out of the input-screen-specific code so the native input can reuse them.
2. **Add chat URL suggestions**: wires up the actual feature on the native input chat tab.

#### Description of changes

**1. Shared utilities extracted (commit 1)**

- `DuckAiChatHistoryFeature` settings accessors (`maxUrlSuggestions()`, `maxHistoryCount()`) lifted into a new `DuckAiChatHistoryFeatureExt.kt` so both surfaces can read the same toggle config.
- The `debounceExceptFirst` flow operator pulled out of `InputScreenViewModel` into `Flows.kt` for reuse.
- `ChatSuggestionsReader` / `ChatSuggestionsNativeReader` updated to consume the new ext functions instead of inlining the settings parse.

**2. Native input chat-tab URL suggestions (commit 2)**

- `NativeInputModeWidgetViewModel` gains `fetchChatTabSuggestions(query, chatSuggestionsEnabled)`, which fetches chat history and URL suggestions in parallel and applies the same filter set + cap as the input screen.
- New `NativeInputChatSuggestionsBinder` builds the chat-tab `ConcatAdapter` (chat history → divider → URL suggestions → divider → "Search for [query]") and exposes a `submit()` that updates all sub-adapters, plus a commit callback fired once the chat-history `ListAdapter` diff has been dispatched.
- `NativeInputModeWidget.bindChatSuggestions` is rebuilt around the binder. 
- `NativeInputManager` propagates the new click hooks up to `BrowserTabFragment` via `NativeInputCallbacks.onChatUrlSuggestionClicked`.
- Pixel parity with the input screen for both selection paths:
  - Chat URL suggestion → `fireAutocompletePixel`.
  - Chat history → `DUCK_CHAT_RECENT_CHAT_SELECTED_(PINNED_)?(COUNT|DAILY)`.
- Unit tests added/updated in `NativeInputModeWidgetViewModelTest` and `BrowserTabViewModelTest`.

### Steps to test this PR

#### 1. First-time entry into chat tab on a new tab

- [ ] Open a new tab. Tap the omnibar to open the native input.
- [ ] Switch to the **Chat** tab.
- [ ] Confirm that the suggestions list shows recent chat history at the top (if any chat history exists). Empty otherwise.
- [ ] Confirm there are no URL suggestions and no "Search for …" row when the input is empty.

#### 2. Typing on the chat tab

- [ ] Open the native input on a new tab and switch to **Chat**.
- [ ] Type in the input field
- [ ] Confirm the list contains: chat history (if any) → divider → URL suggestions (max 3, only bookmarks / history / switch-to-tab / URL search results) → divider → "Search for” row.

#### 3. Selecting a chat-tab URL suggestion

- [ ] On the chat tab, type until URL suggestions appear, then tap one (bookmark / history / switch-to-tab).
- [ ] Confirm the native input dismisses and the URL loads (or tab switches for switch-to-tab suggestions).
- [ ] Confirm `m_autocomplete_click_*` pixel fires with parameters reflecting the selected item

#### 4. Selecting "Search for [query]" on the chat tab

- [ ] On the chat tab, type a query that doesn't match a URL.
- [ ] Tap the "Search for [query]" row at the bottom.
- [ ] Confirm the native input dismisses and the query is submitted as a search.

#### 5. Tab switch interactions

- [ ] On the chat tab with suggestions visible, switch to the **Search** tab. Confirm the chat suggestions list is replaced by the standard search-tab autocomplete (or hidden if there's nothing to show).
- [ ] Switch back to **Chat**. Confirm chat suggestions reappear and are not affected by stale search-tab state.

#### 6. Settings gates

- [ ] Disable "Show chat suggestions" in DuckChat settings.
- [ ] Open native input, switch to **Chat**, type a query.
- [ ] Confirm chat history is **not** shown, but URL suggestions and "Search for [query]" still appear.
- [ ] Re-enable "Show chat suggestions" and confirm chat history reappears.

#### 7. Closing the native input

- [ ] With chat suggestions visible, tap the back button / dismiss the native input.
- [ ] Confirm the suggestions list is hidden cleanly and no leftover content is visible behind the omnibar.
- [ ] Re-open the native input. Confirm the suggestions list starts fresh (no stale items from the previous session).

author: jason-vaughan
body:
## Summary

- Existing TangleClaw installs had stale `~/.tangleclaw/templates/<id>/template.json` — the bundled→runtime copy in `_copyBundledTemplates` was a one-shot at install time, so v3.13.7's `memory-update` addition to `wrap.steps` (and any future bundled template change) never reached anyone who installed before v3.13.7.
- New `_mergeBundledTemplate` in `lib/store.js` self-heals on every server start: deep-merges missing keys, reconciles `wrap.steps` when live is an ordered subsequence of bundled (uncustomized), preserves user-added steps. Same shape of fix as #119 (engine profiles via `_mergeBundledProfile`).
- Tripwire test asserts each bundled template still ships `memory-update` — fires before a future bundle-only regression re-opens the gap.

## Why

Per the issue: every wrap from an existing install continued to omit `memory-update`, so the AI didn't update MEMORY.md until the user noticed. Server restart didn't fix it because the copy is gated on "target has no templates" — it's silently skipped once the runtime dir is populated. The runtime template read path (`store.templates.get`) reads disk fresh per call, but it reads the stale runtime file, not bundled. Needed an active reconciler, not just a fresh read.

## Notes on contract

The merger is **additive-only** by design — it cannot distinguish "user is on a stale install" from "user deliberately removed an entry." A user who explicitly trims a `wrap.steps` step that bundled still ships will see it re-added on next server start. Documented in JSDoc and pinned by a regression test so the trade-off is deliberate. Mirrors `_mergeBundledProfile`'s contract from #119.

## Critic findings addressed

- M1 (missing CHANGELOG entry) — added under `[Unreleased]`.
- M2 (no tripwire for bundled templates shipping `memory-update`) — added.
- S1 (silent overwrite of intentional user deletion) — JSDoc note + pinning regression test.
- S4 (busy-wait in idempotency test) — replaced with `fs.utimesSync` to backdate mtime.
- S3 (direct unit tests on the lifted helpers) — deferred; would require exporting private helpers solely for testing. Integration coverage through `init()` is sufficient.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test 'test/*.test.js'` — 1696 passing (was 1689).
- [x] 7 new tests in `test/store.test.js init`:
  - stale `wrap.steps` (no `memory-update`) → reconciled to bundled
  - user-customized `wrap.steps` (custom step not in bundled) → preserved
  - missing top-level keys → backfilled
  - idempotent across reboots
  - no-rewrite when live matches bundled (mtime check via `fs.utimesSync`)
  - re-adds `wrap.steps` entries the user deliberately removed (pins additive-only contract)
  - bundled templates ship `memory-update` (tripwire)
- [ ] Manual: on a real install with stale runtime templates, restart server and confirm `wrap.steps` adopts `memory-update` without losing user customizations elsewhere.

Fixes #136

author: jspinak
body:
## Summary

Two-line patch to `backend/create_admin.py` that fixes two latent bugs which surfaced together once PR #55 first wired the script into CI.

## Bug 1 — `KeyError: 'Subscription'`

`db.query(User).filter(User.email == email)` walks the User model's relationships through SQLAlchemy's class registry. `User` has a string-based `relationship("Subscription", ...)`, but `app.models.subscription` was never imported when `create_admin.py` ran, so the registry lookup raised `KeyError: 'Subscription'`.

Fix: import `app.db.base_class`, the canonical bulk-import module that Alembic and `run_seed.py` already use. Adding it as a side-effect import (`# noqa: F401`) registers every model in the codebase with `Base.metadata` before the query runs.

## Bug 2 — silent success

```python
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")
    traceback.print_exc()
    db.rollback()
finally:
    db.close()
```

No re-raise, no `sys.exit(1)`. The script exited 0 even when the insert failed. GitHub Actions saw step #12 as `success` despite a full SQLAlchemy traceback in the step output — and downstream `auth.setup.ts` 401'd because the user was never actually inserted. Re-raising after rollback gives CI the correct non-zero exit code.

## How it surfaced

Main run `25406851360` (post-PR #55, headSha `0742e1b2`):

- Step "Create dev user for E2E auth setup": `success` ← lying
- Step "Run frontend E2E tests": `failure` — auth.setup.ts:52 dialog stuck, three POST `/api/v1/auth/jwt/login` → 401, identical to pre-PR-#55
- Hidden in step #12's stdout: `KeyError: 'Subscription'` traceback

## Cascade context

| Layer | Issue | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Alembic graph fork | #43 | merged |
| 2 | RSC `"use client"` boundary | #49 | merged |
| 3 | Seed `PYTHONPATH` | #53 | merged |
| 4 | Dev user not seeded | #55 | merged (but ineffective until this PR) |

author: umarsqureshi
body:
Fixed two bugs prevented Profile OmniFold from producing correct results:

1. Cell 33: test_dataset was built with the full 2-column x_mc (sum + diff of gen pts) after cell 28 redefined it, but wRT_network (n_inputs=4) expects y(2)+x(1)+theta(1)=4 dims. Using x_mc[:,0:1] restores the correct 1-column x.

2. Cell 28: ensemble w function was trained with theta_max=1.5, but the true theta=1.7 lies outside this range. Raised theta_max to 2.0 so the w function covers the true parameter value and theta converges correctly instead of hitting the boundary at 1.9.

author: strokacola
body:
A constellation switch where the new spec keeps the same shape but swaps
the face values (Lyra d6 [1..6] -> Eclipse d6 [0,0,0,1,1,1]) was leaving
the existing dice meshes on the standard pip-cube path. The renderer's
only rebuild triggers were shape changes (`syncDiceShapes`) and per-die
mod-signature changes (`rebuildDie`), so Eclipse's binary face values
never reached `buildD6WithDigits`. Players saw a mix of pips and digits
once Forge happened to rebuild any single die.

Track `faceValues` on the per-die `DieAnim`, rename `syncDiceShapes` to
`syncDiceSpecs`, and rebuild whenever shape OR faces differ from the
spec. Same fix unblocks Fibonacci [1,1,2,3,5,8] and Ophiuchus
[1..5,WILD] for the same scenario.

Tests: regression for the buildDie routing (Eclipse -> digits, plain ->
pips) and a unit test for the new `facesEqual` helper covering canonical
d6, the WILD/BLANK string sentinels, and the Lyra->Eclipse case.
