author: lahavrud
body:
## Summary
Collapse the production deploy artifact to **two SHA-tagged ECR images + one SSM pointer**. The split-artifact model (immutable ECR image vs. mutable S3 configs) is what caused today's 521 — once configs are baked into the image and pinned by SHA, that failure mode is structurally impossible.

## Why
Today's outage: a stale-base merge overwrote `s3://.../deploy/{nginx.conf,docker-compose.deploy.yml}` with pre-HTTPS revisions; nginx came back on port 80; Cloudflare in Full (strict) → 521. PR #289 catches this *specific* regression in CI; this PR removes the split-artifact root cause so future variants can't happen at all.

Stacked on #289 — depends on `scripts/validate_deploy_artifacts.sh` from that PR. Once #289 merges, this PR's diff collapses to just the new work.

## Changes
- **NEW `frontend/Dockerfile`** — multistage `node:20 → nginx:alpine` with `nginx.conf` + `dist/` baked in. New `frontend/.dockerignore` excludes node_modules/dist/tls.
- **`docker-compose.deploy.yml`** — `api`/`worker`/`frontend` images all `:${IMAGE_TAG}`. No `:latest` pin anywhere. Old `nginx` service replaced by `frontend` image; `nginx.conf` and `dist/` bind mounts removed (TLS bind mount stays).
- **`scripts/deploy_ec2.sh`** — resolves `IMAGE_TAG` from env or SSM `CURRENT_SHA`; fetches per-SHA compose; runs `up -d --remove-orphans` to clean up the legacy `nginx` container on first cutover.
- **NEW `scripts/rollback.sh <SHA>`** — verifies per-SHA artifacts in S3 and ECR images exist for the SHA, then puts SSM `CURRENT_SHA` and triggers redeploy via SSM Send-Command. One-command rollback.
- **`scripts/validate_deploy_artifacts.sh`** — gains 6 new assertions: `frontend/Dockerfile` exists and bakes nginx.conf, compose uses `${IMAGE_TAG}` for both images, no `:latest` in compose, deploy script resolves `CURRENT_SHA`, deploy script fetches per-SHA compose path.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — adds `Build and push frontend image` step, switches S3 uploads to per-SHA prefix (`deploy/${{ github.sha }}/`), passes `IMAGE_TAG=${{ github.sha }}` to the SSM command, adds final `Publish CURRENT_SHA to SSM` step that runs only on a successful deploy.

## AWS-side (already applied)
- ECR lifecycle on both `rs-recruitment/api` and `rs-recruitment/frontend` bumped to **keep last 10 tagged images** (~10-deploy rollback window).
- `github-actions-rs-recruitment` role: added `ssm:PutParameter` scoped to `parameter/rs-recruitment/infra/CURRENT_SHA` only; **dropped** stale `s3:DeleteObject` (no longer used after dropping `s3 sync --delete`) and `ssm:ListCommandInvocations` (workflow only calls `GetCommandInvocation`). Least-privilege per role.

## How to Test
- [x] `bash scripts/validate_deploy_artifacts.sh` passes (13 assertions, all green)
- [x] Negative test: revert `${IMAGE_TAG}` to `:latest` in compose → script fails with `no :latest image tag in compose`
- [x] `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean
- [ ] Local docker build of `frontend/Dockerfile` (skipped — docker daemon not running locally; CI builds it)
- [ ] After merge: confirm CI deploy job builds + pushes both images, uploads to per-SHA S3 prefix, SSM Send-Command exports `IMAGE_TAG`, `CURRENT_SHA` populated post-success
- [ ] After first new-system deploy: external smoke `curl -I https://rs-recruiting.com/` returns 200; verify `aws ssm get-parameter --name /rs-recruitment/infra/CURRENT_SHA` matches the deployed SHA
- [ ] Rollback fire drill: `bash scripts/rollback.sh <previous-SHA>` flips `CURRENT_SHA`, site stays 200; `bash scripts/rollback.sh <new-SHA>` rolls forward

## Cutover safety
The new system is opt-in by SHA — first push to `main` after merge builds new images, uploads to a per-SHA prefix the EC2 box has never seen, runs the new `deploy_ec2.sh` from that prefix, and starts the frontend image instead of `nginx:alpine`. Old `:latest` and `s3://.../deploy/` paths are not touched until then; if the new deploy fails, prod stays on the old setup. `--remove-orphans` handles the `nginx` → `frontend` rename so port 443 doesn't double-bind.

## Related Issue
N/A (follow-up to today's incident on #286; #289 added the CI gate, this PR fixes the underlying model).

author: stalephax
body:
### Motivation
- Improve MS‑DOS binary compatibility (notably Word 5.0) by implementing frequently used 8086 opcodes from the opcode-frequency list. 
- Reduce early unsupported-opcode failures so real DOS programs can run further in the emulator.

### Description
- Added handlers in `kernel/mzexe.h` for additional 8086 opcodes: `0x00` (ADD r/m8, r8), `0x01` (ADD r/m16, r16), `0x06`/`0x07`/`0x0E`/`0x16`/`0x17` (segment push/pop ops), `0x08`/`0x0A`/`0x0B`/`0x0C` (OR variants) and `0x20` (AND r/m8, r8). 
- Implementations use `get_effective_address`, `read_rm16`/`write_rm16`, `get_reg8`/`set_reg8` helpers and update flags (`ZF`, `CF`) consistently with the emulator model. 
- Small refactors to OR/AND handling to compute and store the result in a local variable before flag updates to avoid duplicated address calculations and ensure correct `r->ip` advancement.

### Testing
- Ran pattern checks to verify insertions with `rg` (opcode case search) which returned the new handlers and succeeded. 
- Verified working tree and created a commit with `git commit` which completed successfully. 
- No automated unit tests were added or run in this change.

body:
## Day 07: Week-1 cumulative gate — HARD STOP

**Plan reference**: PLAN.md Section 14.5 + Section 11 #3 (hard stop-and-wait at the Week-1 → Week-2 transition).

⚠️ **GATE FAILED on both original and substitute criteria. User adjudication required.**

## Gate result

| # | Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mode 2 (tyre pressure floor on 5 cars) | ✅ PASS |
| 2 | Mode 4 (per-parameter density downgrade) | ✅ PASS |
| 3 | Mode 1 ORIGINAL (BMW H1 MAE ≥ +5%) | ❌ FAIL -7.3% |
| 3a | Mode 1 SUBSTITUTE coverage ≥80% on H1+H3 | ✅ PASS (85.1% / 100%) |
| 3b | Mode 1 SUBSTITUTE Mode-1-sensitive win rate ≥60% | ❌ FAIL 51.7% |
| 4 | Mode 3 (BMW baseline shifts ≥5 params) | ✅ PASS (11 shifted) |
| 5 | No regressions (representative test slice) | ✅ PASS |
| 6 | Composite original (aggregate MAE ≥7%) | ❌ FAIL -7.3% |
| 6 | Composite substitute (0.5×cov + 0.5×win ≥7%) | ❌ FAIL -1.6% |

**3 modes cleanly closed** (2, 3, 4). **Mode 1 mathematically correct but empirically inconclusive** on this corpus.

## Why Mode 1 fails empirically

- **Synthetic case (Day 3)**: 100% improvement on canonical Hockenheim 24×17 vs Spa 6×14.5.
- **95% coverage (Day 5)**: 85.1% on H1, 100% on H3 — calibration is right.
- **Per-parameter wins on physics-relevant subset**: bayes wins clearly on `rear_wing_angle_deg`, `tyre_cold_pressure_kpa`, `damper_lsc_*`, `pushrod_length_offset_rear_mm`.
- **Aggregate held-out MAE**: bayes 7-13% WORSE than v4 baseline on H1/H3 — H1/H3 are outlier setups (H1 has `damper_hsc=5.0` across all 4 corners vs Spa-corpus typical 8-9; `heave_spring=110` vs corpus median 60-70).
- **Mode-1-sensitive win rate**: 51.7% across 29 sensitive parameters — essentially a coin flip on the broader subset.

The math is correct. The corpus's most-recent held-out IBTs are not the converged-fast targets the gate criterion implicitly assumed.

## DEVIATION document committed

`docs/physics-rebuild/DEVIATION_day_07_gate_amendment.md` proposes amending PLAN.md §14.5 criterion #3 to use coverage + win-rate instead of aggregate MAE. The substitute criteria fail too (#3b 51.7%) — the deviation cannot rescue the gate. **Documenting this transparently per the procedurally-correct path** (PLAN.md is immutable per §4.1 F9; DEVIATION docs are the amendment mechanism).

## Three plausible paths

**(A) Accept partial closure and proceed to Week 2** *(my recommendation)*. Modes 2, 3, 4 unambiguously closed; Mode 1 math correct + coverage calibrated; bayes wire-in stays in production. Week 2 adds Mode 5 (new car/track day-zero) which is **independent of Mode 1**. Day 8-14 begins after merge.

**(B) Roll back Day 4 wire-in (PR #74) and proceed to Week 2.** Conservative. Day 3's math stays as a tested module; production PhysicsModel reverts to pre-Day-4 behaviour for `bayes_posteriors`. Smaller surface area. PR #77 amended to include the revert.

**(C) Halt entirely.** Day 8-14 not started; you decide future direction manually.

## NOT done (intentional)

- **No locked tag** (gate failed; PLAN.md §8.3 forbids).

author: jaeyunha
body:
## Summary

- Adds `services` to the root `tsconfig.json` exclude list so `next build` no longer tries to typecheck files outside the Next.js app
- Unblocks Deploy on `main` (failing since #263 introduced `@opensend/mcp`)

## Root cause

`next build` was failing with:

```
./services/api/src/index.ts:1:38
Type error: Cannot find module '@opensend/mcp' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

The Dockerfile's `deps` stage runs `bun install`, which creates `services/api/node_modules/@opensend/mcp` (bun's per-workspace hoisting for deps not depended on by root). The `builder` stage then copies **only** `/app/node_modules` from the deps layer:

```dockerfile
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
```

`services/api/node_modules/` is silently dropped. When `next build` typechecks `services/api/src/index.ts` (matched by the root tsconfig `**/*.ts` glob), TypeScript can't resolve `@opensend/mcp` because the symlink isn't there.

CI's `tsc --noEmit` keeps passing because it runs against the full workspace install (no Docker copy step).

`services/` isn't part of the Next.js app — it's a separate Hono runtime with its own `bun build`. The root tsconfig already excludes `packages/` for the same reason; `services/` was just missed when it was added to the workspace.

## Why this is the right fix

- Matches existing treatment of `packages/`
- Doesn't change runtime behavior — Next.js never shipped or imported services/ code
- Smallest possible change: one line

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`services/api` will no longer be typechecked by the root `tsc --noEmit`. It still has its own `bun build` step, but to keep strict typecheck coverage we should add `services/api/tsconfig.json` and a CI step (`bunx tsc -p services/api`). Filing as a separate task.

## Test plan

- [x] Local `bunx tsc --noEmit --pretty false` passes
- [ ] CI `Typecheck (full project)` passes
- [ ] Deploy workflow advances past the typecheck step on the merge to main

author: pacnpal
body:
## Phase 2: Proxy listener with single hardcoded upstream

Builds out the HTTP CONNECT plus forward proxy and the SOCKS5 listener,
each routed through a single hardcoded upstream (the first one in
config). Phase 3 will swap that out for a priority pool.

### What's done

- `internal/upstream` package: `Upstream` interface plus `direct`, `http`
  (CONNECT), and `socks5` impls. Factory `New(cfg, timeout)` covers each
  kind and rejects unknown ones.
- `internal/listener` package: HTTP listener (CONNECT hijack plus forward
  proxy with hop-by-hop and Proxy-* header stripping) and SOCKS5 listener
  (`armon/go-socks5` wired to the upstream's Dial). Both expose `Ready()`
  for bind-completion signalling and `Shutdown(ctx)` for graceful drain
  bounded by the caller's context, force-closing tunnels that exceed it.
- `cmd/tunnelsmith` boots both listeners with `errgroup` and shuts them
  down on SIGINT or SIGTERM with a 30s drain. The `--version` and
  `--print-config` short-circuit paths still exit before any socket bind,
  so the existing CI smoke steps stay fast.
- `deploy/docker-compose.example.yml` plus `deploy/tunnelsmith.example.toml`:
  minimal stack that CI brings up to exercise the listeners against the
  built image.
- README "Quick start" with the two `curl` commands.
- Listener tests cover HTTP forward, CONNECT, SOCKS5, and shutdown drain;
  pass under `-race` in 1.6s.

### How to verify

- Locally:
  - `make lint` (0 issues)
  - `go test ./... -count=1 -race` (config + listener packages green)
  - `make build && ./bin/tunnelsmith --config examples/tunnelsmith.toml`
    binds `:8080` and `:1080`; SIGINT shuts down cleanly.
- In CI (per ADR-001, image build and run are CI-only):
  - `docker` job builds `tunnelsmith:ci`, brings up
    `deploy/docker-compose.example.yml`, waits for ports 8080 and 1080
    to accept TCP, then runs `curl --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080
    https://example.com` and `curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080
    https://example.com`. Both must return 2xx for the job to pass.

### Docs updated

- [x] README (Quick start)
- [x] CHANGELOG (Phase 2 section)
- [x] `_planning/tunnelsmith-build-plan.md` checkboxes (gitignored)

### Quality gates

- [x] `make lint` clean (0 issues)
- [x] `make test` passes (config + listener; verbose listener output in
      commit `3799452`)
- [x] Docker image built successfully by CI (run id 25556892611)
- [x] CI green (lint, test, build, docker including integration steps,
      all `success`)

### Notes on dependency choices

- `armon/go-socks5` is pinned to the last commit on `master`
  (`v0.0.0-20160902184237-e75332964ef5`). The repo has no tagged
  releases; this is the canonical pseudo-version `go get @latest`
  resolves to.
- `golang.org/x/net` is pinned to `v0.35.0`. Newer releases raise the
  Go directive past `go 1.22` and would either force a toolchain bump
  or fail under CI's pinned `setup-go: 1.22`.
- `golang.org/x/sync v0.10.0` for `errgroup`, same compatibility reason.

author: smaramwbc
body:
## Why

Real user feedback: dragged \`Statewave Admin.app\` from the v0.1.0 \`.dmg\` to \`/Applications\`, double-clicked, hit:

> **„Statewave Admin" ist beschädigt und kann nicht geöffnet werden.**
> Es empfiehlt sich, das Objekt in den Papierkorb zu bewegen.

That's macOS Sequoia (15+) Gatekeeper. The README told them to "right-click → Open the first time" — but **Sequoia removed that escape hatch for unsigned apps**. The correct fix is to strip the \`com.apple.quarantine\` extended attribute via \`xattr -cr\`.

The CLI was also under-documented: no install instructions at all, even though it hits the same Gatekeeper trap on macOS when downloaded via a browser.

## What changes

- **macOS first-launch instruction** is now \`xattr -cr "/Applications/Statewave Admin.app"\` (primary), with a note that right-click → Open also works on macOS 14 and earlier.
- **CLI section** now has step-by-step install instructions for macOS / Linux / Windows, including the same \`xattr -cr\` step for the macOS CLI binary.

No behavioural changes — just docs that match what users actually need to do.

author: ch4r10t33r
body:
## Problem
Peer-supplied SSZ with invalid offset tables could slice past the buffer and **panic** during `deserialize` (struct variable fields, variable `[]T`, variable arrays, and `utils.List` decode). See [zeam#843](https://github.com/blockblaz/zeam/issues/843).

## Change
- **Variable arrays**: require minimum length, aligned offset prefix, prefix within buffer, `start <= end`, monotonic offsets.
- **Variable `[]T`**: validate first/second offsets, item count, and each subsequent offset read before slicing.
- **Structs**: bounds-check every fixed-field read and variable-field slice; enforce `start <= end`, offsets within buffer, monotonicity, and `indices[0] == i` for the first variable field.
- **Unions**: require `serialized.len >= 1` before reading the selector byte.
- **`utils.List.sszDecode`**: fixed-size items reject ragged length and `n > N`; dynamic path bounds-checks the offset-prefix length before slicing.

## Tests / tooling
- Two regression tests for malformed struct payloads.
- `build.zig.zon`: `minimum_zig_version = "0.16.0"` (matches CI; satisfies anyzig when present).

## Downstream
After merge, zeam can switch from a vendored copy back to a `build.zig.zon` `git+` dependency on the new commit.

author: amm1rr
body:
### Overview
This PR implements an **Owner-Aware TTS Cleanup** system to prevent cross-context audio interruptions. 

### Key Changes
- **Background Logic**: Added ownership verification in `TTSStateManager` and updated stop handlers to respect the `stopOnlyIfOwner` flag.
- **UI Integration**: Updated `Popup`, `Sidepanel`, `Mobile Sheet`, and `WindowsManager` to use the new cleanup logic during closure/unmount.
- **Documentation**: Updated technical guides for TTS, FAB, and Mobile Support to reflect this architectural change.

### Impact
Closing a UI element (like the popup) will no longer stop TTS audio initiated by another context (like the Desktop FAB), while still maintaining the `Exclusive Playback` rule for user-initiated actions.

## Correction du rapport QA — Batch 1

Résolution des 14 anomalies identifiées dans l'audit QA sur la v2 (`feat/v2` à `c6853b1`). Branche partie de `feat/v2`, **un commit atomique par bug** (15 commits + 1 chore + 1 test).

### Statut par bug

| ID | Sévérité | Titre | Statut |
|---|---|---|---|
| BUG-005 | 🟠 Majeur | Overflow horizontal mobile | ✅ |
| BUG-002 | 🟠 Majeur | Toast déborde avec nom long | ✅ |
| BUG-007 | 🟠 Majeur | 503 occasionnel sur `mapbox/standard` | ✅ |
| BUG-001 | 🟡 Mineur | Doublons de favoris autorisés | ✅ |
| BUG-003 | 🟡 Mineur | Suppression sans confirmation | ✅ |
| BUG-004 | 🟡 Mineur | Renommage via `prompt()` natif | ✅ |
| BUG-006 | 🟡 Mineur | Pas d'indicateur de focus | ✅ (mostly fixed in Phase 5, finition ici) |
| BUG-008 | 🟡 Mineur | Escape ne vide pas la recherche | ✅ |
| BUG-009 | 🟡 Mineur | Pas de `maxLength` sur input nom | ✅ |
| BUG-010 | 🟡 Mineur | « Aller » ferme le panneau | ✅ |
| BUG-011 | 🔵 Cosmétique | Pas de `<h1>` sur la page | ✅ |
| BUG-012 | 🔵 Cosmétique | Pas de retour si géoloc refusée | ✅ |
| BUG-013 | 🔵 Cosmétique | Preset URL invalide silencieux | ✅ |
| BUG-014 | 🔵 Cosmétique | Cibles tactiles trop petites mobile | ✅ |

### Highlights techniques

**Vague 1 (majeurs)**
- **BUG-005** : `.dir-panel` débordait à 320px (`left: 80px` + `width: min(92vw, 320px)` = 374px). Cap desktop : `width: min(320px, calc(100vw - 96px))`. Mobile : `left: 8/right: 8`.
- **BUG-002** : `.toast` passe de pill à `border-radius: 14px` + `max-width: min(420px, calc(100vw - 32px))` + `word-break: break-word`. Nouveau util `truncate(name, 40)` côté JS.
- **BUG-007** : handler `map.on('error')` étendu pour détecter les 5xx / URL `/styles/v1/` / message `style`. Toast non-bloquant + `setStyle('mapbox/standard')` après 3s, garde-fou via flag `styleRetried`.

**Vague 2 (mineurs)**
- **BUG-001** : `findByName` case-insensitive dans `favorites.ts`, caller refuse + toast `favDuplicate` + `select()`.
- **BUG-003** : `showActionToast` retournant `Promise<boolean>` dans `ui/toast.ts`. Pattern undo : `<li>` masqué optimistement, `remove()` à 5s sans clic.
- **BUG-004** : édition inline (swap `<span>` ↔ `<input>`), Enter/blur valident, Escape annule.
- **BUG-006** : `#search-input:focus:not(:focus-visible) { outline: none }` au lieu de `outline: none` brut.
- **BUG-008** : Escape sorti de la guard `list.hidden`. Comportement 2-temps.
- **BUG-009** : `maxlength: 80` sur `nameInput`.
- **BUG-010** : `panel.close()` retiré du handler `goBtn`.

**Vague 3 (cosmétiques)**
- **BUG-011** : `<h1 class="sr-only" data-i18n="appTitle">` + util CSS standard.
- **BUG-012** : `geolocate.on('error')`. Code 1 → `geolocDenied`, autres → `geolocUnavailable`.
- **BUG-013** : nouveau `parseHashWithErrors` permissif. Si seul le preset est invalide → fallback `'dusk'` + `errors.push('invalidPreset')`. Console.warn + toast au boot.
- **BUG-014** : `@media (max-width: 600px)` impose `min-width/height: 44px` aux boutons interactifs (WCAG 2.5.5).

### Tests

| Métrique | Avant | Après |
|---|---|---|
| Tests unit | 77 | **91** (+14) |
| Tests E2E | 1 | **8** (+7 dans `qa-regression.spec.ts`) |
| App code (gzip) | 13.03 KB | **14.08 KB** (3.5% du budget) |

Les nouveaux tests unit couvrent `truncate` (×5), `findByName` (×4), `parseHashWithErrors` (×5).

Le spec E2E `qa-regression.spec.ts` (workflow_dispatch en CI pour préserver le quota Mapbox) couvre les 7 critères imposés par le rapport QA :
1. No horizontal overflow sur 5 viewports
2. Nom 200 chars → pas overflow
3. Doublon refusé
4. Tab focus → outline visible
5. Escape ×2 → input vidé
6. maxLength 80
7. URL preset invalide → app stable + warn

### Vérifications locales
```
✓ npm run typecheck       (frontend + server)
✓ npm run lint            (0 erreur, 0 warning)
✓ npm test                (91/91 passing)
✓ npm run build           (14.08 KB app + 474 KB mapbox-gl)
```

- [src/styles.css](src/styles.css) — fixes responsive + a11y + 44px mobile
- [src/favorites-ui.ts](src/favorites-ui.ts) — BUG-001, 002, 003, 004, 009, 010

## Resumo

Adiciona ADR-0050 (status `proposed`) formalizando GitHub Container Registry como registry institucional das imagens da `uniplus-api` e a estratégia de tagging.

## Contexto

Pré-requisito da **Fase 5** (deploy das apps no cluster standalone): os ApplicationSets do ArgoCD aguardam imagens publicadas em `ghcr.io/unifesspa-edu-br/uniplus-api-*`. Hoje o repositório tem `docker/Dockerfile.{selecao,ingresso}` + CI de build/test verde, mas nenhum workflow de publish nem convenção formalizada.

A organização já valida GHCR em produção via imagem composta `ghcr.io/unifesspa-edu-br/uniplus-keycloak:1.x` (Keycloak 26.5.7 + JAR `cpf-matcher`). Reaproveitar GHCR mantém a esteira homogênea.

## Decisões binding

- **Registry:** `ghcr.io/unifesspa-edu-br/<imagem>`
- **Naming:** `uniplus-api-{selecao,ingresso,portal}` (portal entra após #336)
- **Tags:** `sha-<7>`, `<branch-sanitizado>`, `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` em git tag, `latest` apenas em `main`
- **Multi-arch:** somente `linux/amd64` (ARM deferido)
- **Login:** `GITHUB_TOKEN` (sem PAT)
- **SBOM/cosign attestation:** deferidos como follow-up
- **Visibilidade:** pública (espelha o repositório)

## Pareada com

`uniplus-web/docs/adrs/0020-registry-ghcr-e-tagging.md` — mesma decisão simétrica para frontends.

## Implementação

Story #337 (sub-issue de Feature #7) implementa o workflow `publish-images.yml` consumindo as decisões deste ADR.

## Promoção a `accepted`

Padrão do projeto: ADR fica `proposed` no merge e é promovido a `accepted` em commit posterior, após o primeiro publish verde da Story #337 (ver precedente em #0049 / A.1).

- [x] `bash tools/adr-lint/validate.sh` passou (50 ADRs)

author: fatih-koca
body:
## Summary

Pauses the libretro core's run loop while the in-game menu (or the core-load-failure dialog) is on screen. Previously the menu was cosmetic — the CADisplayLink kept ticking, \`retro_run\` kept advancing the game, and audio kept producing while the user thought the game was frozen.

## Why

User reported: \"durdurma ekranına geçince oyunun durmaması, panel ekrana geliyor herşey çalışıyor ama oyun arkada devam ediyor\". Save state actions taken from the menu were also landing on a different frame than the one the user saw on screen, because frames kept advancing between menu-open and save-state-tap.

## How

\`MetalViewRepresentable\` now carries an \`isPaused\` Bool that SwiftUI sets to \`showMenu || coreLoadFailed\`. \`MetalGameViewController.setPaused(_:)\` flips \`displayLink.isPaused\` accordingly.

While paused:
- \`tick()\` no longer fires → \`retro_run\` is not called → game state freezes
- The renderer is frame-driven, so the last drawn frame stays on screen unchanged
- The audio ring buffer drains over ~100 ms; the existing underrun fade in \`AudioEngine\` handles the silence boundary cleanly
- On resume, the very next tick runs the next frame — no state restoration is needed

## Test plan

- [ ] Open an imported ROM, start gameplay, tap pause/menu — game freezes on screen, audio fades out smoothly within a heartbeat
- [ ] Close the menu — game resumes from exactly where it stopped, audio fades back in
- [ ] Tap pause, take a save state — the saved frame matches the frame frozen on screen (this used to drift)
- [ ] Built-in Glowchase demo still pauses via its own logic (unchanged path)

## Summary

- Implements the doc 184 Torghut execution-trusted profit repair settlement ledger as an additive zero-notional runtime projection.
- Publishes deterministic repair lots through `/trading/status`, `/trading/health`, `/readyz`, and `/trading/consumer-evidence` so stale or unresolved profit evidence is visible before live enablement.
- Extends Jangar consumer-evidence parsing and negative-evidence routing with settlement ledger refs, aggregate state, repair lot ids, and blocker reason codes.
- Updates Torghut docs and the current source-of-truth guide to cite doc 184 as the active runtime requirement after the doc 183 freshness work.

## Related Issues

None. Requirement provenance: `docs/torghut/design-system/v6/184-torghut-execution-trusted-profit-repair-settlement-2026-05-08.md`, companion design `docs/agents/designs/180-jangar-execution-trust-debt-retirement-and-profit-repair-settlement-2026-05-08.md`, and the `torghut-quant` runtime objective to increase routeable post-cost profit evidence and live trading readiness without weakening capital safety.

## Breaking Changes

## Risk, Rollback, And Release Note

Design reference: doc 184 and companion design 180 require Jangar execution trust debt to be represented as zero-notional repair settlement before Torghut can claim live profit readiness. This PR ships the additive runtime ledger, Jangar projection, regression tests, and documentation alignment.

author: hartsock
body:
## Summary

Final piece of the path to PyPI 0.1.0. Three layered changes:

### 1. `scrybe.ai` metapackage architecture

`scrybe` is taken on PyPI by an unrelated project, so the umbrella PyO3 library can't ship under that name. Pivoting to a metapackage:

```
scrybe.ai           ← thin metapackage, deps on the four below
├── scrybe-py        (renamed from `scrybe`; PyO3 library; `import scrybe`)
├── scrybe-cli       (maturin bin wheel — `scrybe` command)
├── scrybe-mcp-server (maturin bin wheel)
└── scrybe-mermaid   (PyO3 library — PNG iTXt codec)
```

`pip install scrybe.ai` pulls in the full Python toolkit. Users who only want one piece can `pip install scrybe-cli` directly. Tauri desktop app remains a separate GitHub Release artifact.

`import scrybe` keeps working — distribution name and import name are independent. The maturin config in `scrybe-py/pyproject.toml` already pointed at `module-name = "scrybe._rust"` and `python-source = "python"` (where `python/scrybe/__init__.py` lives), so renaming the **distribution** to `scrybe-py` doesn't change the **import**. Same pattern as `pillow` (distribution) → `PIL` (import).

### 2. Wheel matrix expanded + metapackage build job

| Job | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `build-wheels` matrix | `[scrybe-cli, scrybe-mcp-server]` × 3 OSes = 6 wheels | `[scrybe-py, scrybe-cli, scrybe-mcp-server, scrybe-mermaid]` × 3 OSes = 12 wheels |
| `build-meta` (NEW) | — | Single ubuntu job builds pure-Python `scrybe.ai` (sdist + noarch wheel) with hatchling |
| `publish-pypi` | depends on `build-wheels` | depends on `[build-wheels, build-meta]`; uploads everything in one OIDC batch |

### 3. Dual-trigger release flow (release/** branches + v* tags)

- **Trigger expansion**: workflow now fires on both `v*` tag pushes AND `release/**` branch pushes. Branch pushes let you stage a release build (e.g. on `release/v0.1.0`) and verify wheels publish before tagging.
- **Tauri build is tag-only**: `build-app` gated on `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')`. `tauri-action` creates a GitHub Release named after `github.ref_name`, which only makes sense for a tag like `v0.1.0`. Branch pushes therefore ship PyPI wheels only — no GitHub Release.
- **Idempotent publish**: added `skip-existing: true` to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` so branch-push-then-tag-push for the same version doesn't error on the second upload.

## Files

- **`scrybe-meta/`** (new) — pure-Python metapackage. `pyproject.toml` (hatchling), `README.md`, `src/scrybe_ai/__init__.py` (tiny stub module so the wheel has a valid distribution anchor).
- **`scrybe-py/pyproject.toml`** — `name = \"scrybe\"` → `name = \"scrybe-py\"`. Maturin config unchanged.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — matrix expansion + new `build-meta` job + `publish-pypi` waits on both + dual trigger + tag-gated Tauri + idempotent publish.
- **`README.md`** — install instructions reflect the new layout.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — release-process snippet updated.

## Local verification (metapackage build)

```
scrybe_ai-0.5.20260507-py3-none-any.whl  ← PEP 503 normalized filename
scrybe_ai-0.5.20260507.tar.gz
```

Wheel metadata reads `Name: scrybe.ai` with the four `Requires-Dist` lines pinned to the workspace version.

## Manual steps after merge — needed before tagging 0.1.0

1. **Register four pending publishers on PyPI** (Owner=`hartsock`, Repo=`scrybe`, Workflow=`release.yml`, Environment=`pypi`):
   - `scrybe-py`
   - `scrybe-cli`
   - `scrybe-mcp-server`
   - `scrybe-mermaid`
2. **Tighten existing `scrybe.ai` pending publisher** — set Environment from `(Any)` → `pypi`.
3. **Create the `pypi` GitHub Actions environment** at https://github.com/hartsock/scrybe/settings/environments. Deployment-branches rule should be **Selected branches and tags** with BOTH:
   - tag pattern: `v*`
   - branch pattern: `release/**`

After these are in place, either `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0` (full release) OR `git push origin release/v0.1.0` (PyPI-only stage) drives the workflow end-to-end.

## Summary
  ### Why     
  BFF/serverBuild/setupTsRuntime hardcode `<appDir>/tsconfig.json`. Projects
  needing `moduleResolution: "NodeNext"` for server code (e.g. subpath-export                                                  
  deps) must flip the *root* tsconfig to NodeNext, breaking frontend                                                           
  type-checking in `src/` (lodash-es ESM imports, dynamic `import()` without                                                   
  `.js`).                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                               
  ### What                                                                                                                      
  File-presence convention: prefer `tsconfig.server.json` if present, else                                                     
  `tsconfig.json`. Centralized in `@modern-js/utils.resolveServerTsconfig`                                                     
  and called from 3 server-side stages.

body:
## Summary

Migrates the entire Squiggle solution from .NET Framework 4.5.1 to .NET 9 with SDK-style projects.

Closes #26

## Changes

### Project System
- Converted all 12 .csproj files from legacy format to SDK-style
- Created `Directory.Build.props` for shared build properties
- Removed `packages.config` files (NuGet PackageReference used instead)
- Removed `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` files (using shared assembly info)
- Excluded `Squiggle.Setup` (WiX installer) from solution

### .NET Core Compatibility Fixes
- **NetMQ**: Updated from v3 to v4 API (removed `NetMQContext`, use typed socket constructors, `SendFrame`, `TryReceive`)
- **WCF removal**: Removed all unused `System.ServiceModel` imports; replaced `SynchronizedCollection<T>` with thread-safe `Collection<T>`
- **FluidKit**: Inlined BSD-licensed DragDrop source files (external DLL not .NET Core compatible)
- **MEF**: Added `System.ComponentModel.Composition` NuGet package
- **SyndicationFeed**: Added `System.ServiceModel.Syndication` package for RSS update checker
- **System.Drawing**: Added `System.Drawing.Common` package
- **Windows Services**: Replaced `ManagedInstallerClass` (removed in .NET Core) with `sc.exe` instructions; removed legacy `ProjectInstaller` files
- **LINQ**: Removed custom `Append<T>` extension (now built-in)
- **WPF entry point**: Disabled auto-generated App definition for custom Main method

### CI
- Added GitHub Actions CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- Builds on `windows-latest` with .NET 9 SDK

<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Po co

Zamiast klikania w phpMyAdmin (drop tabel) + dwóch osobnych URL-i (`apply_migrations_chain.php`, `setup_database.php`) + ręcznego `INSERT INTO sh_tenant/sh_users` — **jeden URL z guziczkami**, chroniony tym samym kluczem co `keep_only_owner_admin_users.php`.

URL produkcyjny: `https://slicehub.net/scripts/install_panel.php`
Klucz trzymany w `core/local_secrets.php` (gitignored, pattern jak w istniejących skryptach).

## Co potrafi panel

| Sekcja | Akcja | Komentarz |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Stan połączenia** | `health` | env-y `SLICEHUB_DB_*`, wersja MySQL, ilość tabel/tenantów/userów. Zera podświetlone na czerwono (Alert 86 / Konstytucja §6). |
| **2. Instalacja krokowa** | `init_schema` | Wgrywa `001_init_slicehub_pro_v2.sql` z auto-stripem `CREATE DATABASE` / `USE` (uti.pl nie pozwala). |
| | `run_chain` | Łańcuch `004–044` z `_migrations_chain.php`. Znane WARN-y (`010` Duplicate column, `037` 1901 GENERATED) oznaczane osobno, nie liczone jako FAIL. |
| **3. Pełny reset (DESTRUKCYJNE)** | `drop_all` | Drop wszystkich tabel + widoków + procedur + funkcji + eventów. Wymaga confirm `"USUWAM"`. |
| | `full_install` | Drop + 001 + chain w jednym kliknięciu. Wymaga confirm `"USUWAM I INSTALUJĘ"`. |
| **4. Tenant** | `list_tenants` / `create_tenant` | Lista + jedno pole na nazwę. |
| **5. Owner / admin** | `create_owner` | **bcrypt hashowany serwerowo** (`PASSWORD_DEFAULT`). User wpisuje plain. Walidacja: hasło ≥8, role ∈ `{owner, admin, manager}`. |
| **6. Użytkownicy** | `list_users` | Lista per tenant (z barierą `tenant_id` per Konstytucja §2). |
| | `change_password` | Zmiana hasła istniejącego konta — też bcrypt serwerowo. |

## Bezpieczeństwo (Konstytucja §2 + reszta)

- **Auth:** każde wywołanie wymaga `X-Script-Key` = `SLICEHUB_SCRIPT_KEY` z `core/local_secrets.php`. Bez tego 403. Klucz w sessionStorage przeglądarki, NIE w URL → nie wycieka do access logów.
- **Multi-tenancy (§2):** każde zapytanie cross-tenant ma barierę `WHERE tenant_id = :tid`. Brak tenant_id = błąd, nie wyciek. Dowód testem (F8 / I3): `change_password` z cudzym `tenant_id` zwraca "Nie znaleziono", baza nieruszona (`password_verify` na starym hashu nadal `true`).
- **Cross-silo (§9):** w panelu nie ma JOIN-ów cross-silo. Wszystkie tabele to wewnątrz silosu `sh_`.
- **JSON API (§5):** `{success, message, data}`, action-based router (`switch($action)`). Zero HTML leakage przed JSON-em (output buffer flush w `panel_json`).
- **Confirm-token na destrukcyjne akcje:** drop/full_install nie zadziała bez prompt-em wpisanej frazy potwierdzającej.
- **DB connection osobno od `core/db_config.php`:** `db_config.php` robi `die()` przy błędzie — panel chcemy żeby działał jako narzędzie diagnostyczne nawet gdy normalna apka pada. Dlatego panel sam łączy się przez PDO i pokazuje pełny `error_log`-owy powód błędu.
- **SQL injection — odporny.** Wszystkie inputy idą przez prepared statements. Próba `Pizza'); DROP TABLE sh_users;--` w nazwie tenanta zapisuje się jako literał, baza nadal żyje.
- **Friendly PDO errors** — nowa funkcja `panel_friendly_pdo_message()` mapuje SQLSTATE 1062/1146 na czytelny PL (np. „login zajęty — sh_users.username jest unikalny globalnie, sufiksuj id tenanta"), zamiast surowego `SQLSTATE[23000]`.
- **Stack (§3):** vanilla JS + Tailwind via CDN. Zero Node/npm/React.

## Co się jeszcze zmieniło (refactor — snajper)

- `scripts/_migrations_chain.php` (NEW) — czysta tablica plików migracji `004–044`, jedno źródło prawdy.
- `scripts/apply_migrations_chain.php` — zamiast hardcoded `$chain = [...]` (38 linii) jest teraz `$chain = require __DIR__ . '/_migrations_chain.php';`.
- Audyt CLI nadal działa: `php scripts/apply_migrations_chain.php --audit` → `OK: łańcuch zgodny z plikami na dysku`.

## Krytyczny audyt logiki (po pierwszym mergeable commit)

Zrobiłem drugą rundę testów na świeżej, pustej bazie (`drop_all` → wszystkie scenariusze) żeby znaleźć szorstkości. Znalazłem 4, naprawiłem w commit `70c31b5`:

| # | Problem | Co zrobiłem |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `list_tenants` na pustej bazie → `SQLSTATE[42S02] Base table not found` | Nowa `panel_table_exists()` + flaga `schema_missing` w response. UI pokazuje przyjazny pill „Brak schematu — uruchom najpierw instalację". |
| 2 | `list_users` na pustej bazie → to samo | Identyczny pattern z `schema_missing`. |
| 3 | `create_owner` z duplikatem login → surowy `SQLSTATE[23000]` | `panel_friendly_pdo_message()` mapuje 1062 + `uq_users_username` na czytelne PL z wyjaśnieniem, że schemat ma globalnie unikalny username. |
| 4 | Po `init_schema` lub `run_chain` dropdown tenantów się nie odświeżał automatycznie | JS auto-refresh po sukcesie obu akcji (wcześniej tylko po `full_install`). |

Plus jedno **ostrzeżenie w UI**: `001` robi `DROP TABLE` tylko swoich tabel — na nie-pustej bazie (z chain) zostawia mieszany stan (94 tabele zamiast 92). Sekcja 2 mówi teraz wprost: na czystą instalację użyj „Pełny reset".

## Testy (lokalna MariaDB 10.11.14)

End-to-end backend (curl + JSON API):

| Krok | Wynik |
|---|---|
| `health` bez auth | `403` ✓ |
| `health` z auth (czysta baza) | `tables=0, tenants=0, users=0`, env-y wszystkie green ✓ |
| `drop_all` bez confirm | rejected ✓ |
| `full_install` z confirm | `DROP: 0, INIT 001: 38 tabel, CHAIN: 37 OK / 0 hard-fail`, finalnie 92 tabele ✓ |
| `health` po instalacji | `tables=92, tenants=1` (Demo Tenant z migracji), `users=0` ✓ |
| `create_tenant("SliceHub Test 2")` | `tenant_id=2` ✓ |
| `create_owner(t=1, owner_t1, superSecret123)` | `user_id=1`, hash w bazie `$2y$10$...` długość 60 ✓ |
| `password_verify('superSecret123', hash)` | `true` ✓ |
| `password_verify('zleHaslo', hash)` | `false` ✓ |
| `change_password(t=1, owner_t1, NoweHaslo456!)` | nowe hasło verify=true, stare verify=false ✓ |
| Walidacja hasło `"short"` | rejected: "min. 8 znaków" ✓ |
| Walidacja role `"superuser"` | rejected: "owner, admin, manager" ✓ |
| `drop_all` z confirm | 89 tabel usuniętych, baza pusta ✓ |
| `init_schema` osobno | 38 tabel z 001 ✓ |
| `run_chain` osobno | 37 OK, 0 FAIL, 1 WARN (znany `037` 1901) ✓ |

Audyt drugiej rundy (po fixach):

| # | Scenariusz | Wynik |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | `list_tenants` na pustej | `success=true, schema_missing=true, message="Brak schematu — uruchom instalację."` ✓ |
| F2 | `list_users` na pustej | jw. + `users=[]` ✓ |

| F6 | `list_tenants` po instalacji | `schema_missing=false`, count=1 ✓ |
| F7 | role `admin` / `manager` | obie zaakceptowane ✓ |

author: ianjamesburke
body:
Fixes #861.

## What changed

The prior attempt (PR #959) called `render_name_bar_and_dots` inside the `egui::Frame` closure. `TerminalView` fills its background using the full Frame inner area, painting over any name bar text drawn before it in the same layout pass — so the name never appeared even when the pane was named.

**Fix:** paint the name bar directly on `child_ui` **before** `Frame::show`, then `advance_cursor_after_rect` to push the Frame's outer rect below the bar. The Frame's fill and the terminal content inside it can no longer reach the name bar's pixel rows.

Also restores tab dot rendering for unnamed panes in a tab group — the prior attempt accidentally deleted the separate `paint_tab_dots` block without replacing it for the no-name case.

Reverts `render_name_bar_and_dots` back to private — it's no longer called from `app/mod.rs`.

## Breaks if
Named terminal panes don't show their name above the content when zoomed to full screen (Enter key).

author: obiot
body:
## Summary

Adds first-class Capacitor support to the melonJS monorepo:

1. **New package: `@melonjs/capacitor-plugin`** — a `BasePlugin`-style adapter that bridges Capacitor's native lifecycle and hardware-back events into the engine. No engine changes were needed; this is purely an ergonomics layer over the standard `@capacitor/app` events.
2. **`create-melonjs --template capacitor`** — new template flag that scaffolds from a Capacitor-flavored boilerplate (`melonjs/typescript-boilerplate-capacitor`, to be created separately).
3. **Wiki draft** — full Capacitor guide saved to `/tmp/Capacitor.md` locally; needs to be pasted into the `melonjs/melonJS.wiki` repo.

## What the plugin gives you

```ts
plugin.register(CapacitorPlugin, "capacitor", { pauseAudio: true });

class PlayStage extends Stage {
    onResetEvent() {
        bindStageBack(this, (evt) => {
            state.change(state.MENU);
            evt.preventDefault();   // suppress default App.exitApp()
        });
    }
}
```

vs. ~25 lines of raw `App.addListener(...)` boilerplate per game today.

| Feature | API | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Lifecycle | `pauseOnBackground`, `pauseAudio` options | `appStateChange` → `state.pause/resume` |
| Hardware back | `bindStageBack(stage, fn)` / `onBackButton(fn)` | `backButton` → engine event bus, `evt.preventDefault()` to suppress default exit |
| Orientation | `lockOrientation("portrait" \| "landscape")`, `unlockOrientation()` | Lazy wrappers around `@capacitor/screen-orientation` |
| Splash | `hideSplash({ fadeOutDuration })` | Lazy wrapper around `@capacitor/splash-screen` |

`@capacitor/app` is the only required peer dep; orientation and splash deps are optional and dynamically imported only when the corresponding helpers are called.

## Files

- `packages/capacitor-plugin/` — new package, ~150 LOC of source across 8 `src/*.ts` files plus the standard scaffolding (package.json, tsconfigs, scripts, README, CHANGELOG, LICENSE).
- `packages/create-melonjs/` — `--template <name>` flag, version bump 1.0.1 → 1.1.0, README + CHANGELOG.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors.
- [x] `pnpm build` (`packages/capacitor-plugin`) — emits `build/index.js` + `.d.ts` cleanly.
- [x] `pnpm vitest run` — 2933 melonjs tests still pass; no regressions.
- [x] `node packages/create-melonjs/bin/create-melonjs.js` — usage banner shows the new flag and templates.
- [x] `node ... my-game --template bogus` — errors out with the list of known templates.
- [ ] End-to-end iOS/Android scaffold + run (deferred — needs `melonjs/typescript-boilerplate-capacitor` repo to exist).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Create `melonjs/typescript-boilerplate-capacitor` GitHub repo (Vite + melonJS + `@capacitor/*` + `@melonjs/capacitor-plugin` pre-wired). The `--template capacitor` flag will 404 until this repo exists.
- Paste `/tmp/Capacitor.md` into the `melonjs/melonJS.wiki` repo.
- Add a Capacitor logo to the README's "Tools integration" section.

## Summary

**MascotPalette** is exported from BOTH `src/components/mascot/MascotPalette.ts` AND `src/components/theme-a/MascotPalette.ts` — they must stay byte-equal until someone intentionally diverges them. Without a test, a value tweak in one silently mismatches on surfaces consuming the other (off-brand brown on every theme-a mascot, but only on theme-a routes).

**`preferences-state.ts`** split out of `actions/preferences.ts` because Next.js refuses to compile non-async exports from a `'use server'` module. `PREFERENCE_CATEGORIES` (literal-type source) and `DEFAULT_PREFERENCES` (Record) MUST have the same key set — drift means a new category renders no toggle in `/dashboard/preferences`, or an old category leaks a stale default. - Both `V3_PAL` exports have identical key sets

author: unseensnick
body:
## Summary

Two scopes bundled — the planned reader wheel-overscroll feature plus a small detail-page typography polish that wasn't worth its own PR.

### Reader: wheel-event chapter advance at scroll boundaries

In continuous reading modes (Webtoon / Continuous Vertical / Continuous Horizontal), the existing tap-zone and hotkey paths already trigger `ReaderControls.openChapter('previous' | 'next')` at scroll start/end. This adds the wheel path:

- At a boundary, scrolling further in the same direction accumulates up to ~100px; crossing the threshold loads the previous/next chapter.
- Backward advance lands at the previous chapter's end via the existing `ReaderResumeMode.END` plumbing — no behaviour change there.
- Direction reversal resets the accumulator (brushing the boundary doesn't queue an advance).
- An ~800ms cooldown after firing prevents a single scroll gesture from advancing two chapters in a row.
- Gated on `shouldUseInfiniteScroll` so users who opt out aren't surprised.
- Horizontal modes fall back to `deltaX || deltaY`, matching browsers that translate vertical wheel into horizontal scroll on horizontal containers.

New hook at `src/features/reader/viewer/hooks/useReaderWheelOverscrollChapterAdvance.ts`, wired into `ReaderViewer` next to the existing scroll/cursor hooks.

### Manga detail: typography polish

- Title moves from h5 to h4 semibold with tightened line-height + slight negative tracking, so it anchors the page rather than competing with the metadata stack.
- Synopsis caps at 70ch with secondary-text colour and 1.6 line-height (copy was running 100+ characters wide on desktop).
- Genre tags become hairline mono-uppercase pills with a sage-on-hover tint, matching the rest of the redesign.

Backdrop, ResumeFab, and the chapter list intentionally untouched — the existing `mangaThumbnailBackdrop` setting (Settings → Appearance → "Manga thumbnail as background") and the `ResumeFab` floating Continue button already cover what the plan called for; rewriting either was high risk for low gain.

## Test plan

### Reader

- [ ] Webtoon mode: scroll to the very bottom of a chapter, keep wheeling down → next chapter loads after ~100px overscroll.
- [ ] Same chapter: scroll to top, wheel up → previous chapter loads, lands at its **last page** (paginated) or **bottom** (continuous).
- [ ] Direction reversal mid-overscroll resets the accumulator (no rogue advance).
- [ ] Cooldown after firing — a continued scroll gesture doesn't fire twice.
- [ ] First chapter, top boundary: wheel up does nothing.
- [ ] Last chapter, bottom boundary: wheel down does nothing (existing behaviour preserved).
- [ ] Disable "infinite scroll" in reader settings → wheel overscroll stops triggering chapter advance.
- [ ] Single Page / Double Page modes — wheel overscroll does **not** apply (only continuous modes are affected).
- [ ] Existing hotkeys (`,`/`.`, `[`/`]`, etc.) and tap-zones still advance chapters as before.

### Manga detail

- [ ] Title anchors visually at the top of the metadata column (h4-sized, tighter).
- [ ] Synopsis caps around 70 characters per line on desktop.
- [ ] Genre tags appear as hairline outlined pills, mono-uppercase, sage on hover.
- [ ] Backdrop unchanged (still gated by the `mangaThumbnailBackdrop` setting).
- [ ] ResumeFab unchanged.

author: dmikalova
body:
fixes #3484 fixes #4917 fixes #2908 fixes #3280

When Mirror Shell copies a creature name onto a token card, `tokenCard()` was looking up by name. This could fail when a copyCard effect overrides `this.name`, causing the wrong token definition (or no token) to be returned.

**Fix:** resolve the token directly from `this.owner.tokenCard` instead of searching all players by name.

**Test:** adds a regression test to `MirrorShell.spec.js` verifying that a Grunt token copied via Mirror Shell retains correct identity and abilities.

> [!NOTE]
> CSS card ring highlighting split into a separate PR: #5113

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core card resolution, house availability, and UI state for all tokens; behavior change is targeted but affects shared `Card`/`Player` paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes token handling when **Mirror Shell** (and similar `copyCard` effects) copy a creature onto a token without breaking game logic or UI.
> 
> **`tokenCard()`** now returns the owning player’s deck token definition (`owner.tokenCard`) instead of scanning all players by `this.name`, which could resolve the wrong card or nothing after `copyCard` overrides the displayed name.
> 
> **House selection** for in-play cards uses `card.getHouses()` on the live instance so tokens respect `copyCard` and enhancements; out-of-play tokens still fall back to the printed token definition.
> 
> **Client summary** sets `copying` only when a non-baseline `copyCard` is active (not the default token self-copy from `MakeTokenCreatureAction`).

author: fede654
body:
## Follow-up to PR #10 (already merged)

Field-test post-merge surfaced que el modelo seguía haciendo cosas raras: fabricaba goto coords ([1,64,518] para player en [-6,81,64]), ignoraba inventory (place_block(oak_log) cuando solo había oak_planks), emitía loops de scan_nearby. Después de varias rondas de patches consumer-side, Fede preguntó: "por qué teniendo la implementación en el repositorio de Mariano, nos estamos encontrando con huecos en la composición de las queries?"

Audit completo contra `Mar-IA-no/deamoncraft-gemma4-andy:examples/eval_with_adapter.py` — la **reference implementation** byte-exact con el SFT training.

## 5 drift points fixed

| # | Drift | Canonical (eval_with_adapter.py) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `guardian_constraints` con 4 fields | 5 fields verbatim — agregamos `executor_filtering: true`, `no_player_harm: true`; quitamos `protected_zone_owner: null` |
| 2 | Sampling: solo `num_predict: 1024` | reference usa `do_sample=False` (greedy); production OLLAMA_USAGE.md usa `temperature: 0.0, num_predict: 512`. Modelfile pins 0.2 → variance suficiente para fabricar coords |
| 3 | `bot_position` / `player_position` floats `[27.3, 79, 56.5]` | training usa block coords integer `[10, 68, 5]`. `Math.floor` aplicado |
| 4 | `nearby_entities` con noise (`item`, `chest_minecart`, `arrow`...) | training usa solo type strings que el modelo conoce: mobs, players, animals. Filter aplicado |
| 5 | Companion intent templating + Path A bug | (a) `build_intent` returnea body verbatim — earlier wrappers como "This is a NAVIGATION command. Emit ONLY..." se interpretaban como user request; (b) `process_command` pasaba el body ya-stripped por `_fuzzy_addresses_me` → false negative → mensaje descartado silenciosamente |

## Por qué importa

Sin alineación byte-exact, cada drift empuja el input off-distribution. Suma → modelo cae a priors. Con `temperature: 0.0` greedy + canonical contract → outputs determinísticos y on-spec.

## Files changed

```
agents/embodied-service/companion.py       | new file (chat-driven companion mode)
agents/embodied-service/lib/defaults.js    | guardian_constraints alineado
agents/embodied-service/lib/dispatcher.js  | menor cleanup
agents/embodied-service/lib/ollama.js      | temperature: 0.0, num_predict: 512
agents/embodied-service/lib/world_state.js | int coords + entity filter + 17-field shape
```

Note: `companion.py` es nuevo y experimental — chat-driven loop que escucha el WebSocket del bot y dispatcha intents del jugador via embodied service. Útil para field-test 1-on-1 mientras se trabaja en el wireup completo del DaemonCraft gateway. No bloquea funcionalidad core; se puede mover a una carpeta `examples/` si preferís.

## Vault

Documentado en mi vault local en `concepts/gemma-andy-canonical-reference.md` con recipe para refrescar mirrors de los docs de Mariano cuando upstream se actualiza.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test test/` — 43/43 pass
- [x] `world_state` byte-exact con `EXAMPLE_USER` de eval_with_adapter.py
- [x] `guardian_constraints` byte-exact con reference
- [ ] Field-test live con player presente (en flight)

author: forrestthump
body:
## Fix Windows compilation: Unix cfg guards and proxy Cargo.toml section ordering

`cargo build` and `cargo test` were both broken on Windows. This PR fixes three distinct root causes.

---

### Bug 1 — `turbomcp-unix` compiled on Windows

`turbomcp-unix` had no platform guard, so it was always compiled. On Windows, `tokio::net::UnixListener` and `tokio::net::UnixStream` don't exist (they're `#[cfg(unix)]`-gated in tokio), causing compile errors.

**Fix:** Added `#![cfg(unix)]` to `turbomcp-unix/src/lib.rs`, gating the entire crate. Then propagated `#[cfg(all(feature = "unix", unix))]` (replacing bare `#[cfg(feature = "unix")]`) through every crate that re-exports or references unix transport types:

- `turbomcp-transport/src/lib.rs` + `config.rs` + `tests/unix_tests.rs`
- `turbomcp-server/src/builder.rs`, `handler.rs`, `transport/mod.rs`
- `turbomcp-client/src/lib.rs`, `prelude.rs`
- `turbomcp-cli/src/transport.rs`

`turbomcp/src/lib.rs` was already using the correct `#[cfg(all(unix, feature = "unix"))]` form.

---

### Bug 2 — `turbomcp-proxy` dependencies accidentally unix-only

`turbomcp-proxy/Cargo.toml` had `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` placed in the **middle** of `[dependencies]`. In TOML, a section header captures everything below it until the next header, so `tokio`, `serde_json`, `bytes`, `axum`, `tracing`, `uuid`, `dashmap`, `secrecy`, and ~40 other direct dependencies were silently unix-only. On Windows, every import of these crates failed with `unresolved import`.

**Fix:** Moved the `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` block to after `[dev-dependencies]`, where it no longer captures unrelated entries.

---

### Bug 3 — proxy examples referenced `BackendTransport::Unix` without a platform guard

Two examples failed to compile on Windows because `BackendTransport::Unix` (correctly gated in bug 1's fix) doesn't exist on non-unix platforms:

- `unix_socket_backend.rs` — entire example is unix-only; added a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` stub `main` and gated the real implementation with `#[cfg(unix)]`
- `schema_export.rs` — added `#[cfg(unix)]` to the `"unix"` match arm; the `other =>` catch-all handles it gracefully on Windows

---

### Result

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo build --workspace` | ❌ | ✅ (requires `protoc` for `turbomcp-grpc`, unchanged) |
| `cargo test --workspace` | ❌ | ✅ (excluding `turbomcp-grpc`) |

Unix socket transport remains fully functional on Linux/macOS — the guards are no-ops on those platforms. Windows developers get access to all other transports (stdio, HTTP, WebSocket, TCP) without any code changes required.

author: oldsheeep3
body:
## 概要

ユーザープロフィール画面の 2 件をまとめて対応した。

1. **修正**: フォロー済みのユーザーのプロフィールを開いてもフォロー済みとして表示されない問題を解消（自分の following リストから target を線形探索する方式に切り替え）。
2. **機能追加**: アイコン画像（AuthCore 経由）とバナー画像（SNS backend `/v1/images`）を画面からアップロードできるようにした。

計画ドキュメント: [`docs/tasks/fix-follow-display-and-add-icon-banner-upload.md`](docs/tasks/fix-follow-display-and-add-icon-banner-upload.md)

## 細かい変更点

### Phase 1: フォロー済み判定の修正
- `src/hooks/useFollowState.ts` (新規): viewer の `/users/{me.sub}/following?limit=50` をページング走査して target sub を線形探索する hook。`{ following: boolean | null, loading, setFollowing }` を返す。null は判定中。未認証 / 自分自身 / abort は早期リターン。エラー時は `false` 倒し + `console.error` のみ。
  - 守りで `MAX_PAGES=20` のガードと、同一 cursor 検出での break を入れて無限ループを防止。
  - viewer × target の判定結果を module-level Map にキャッシュ（`setFollowing` でも書き戻すので楽観反映後の再訪でも整合）。
- `src/routes/UserProfileRoute.tsx`: `firstPost?.followingAuthor` 推定経路を撤去し、`useFollowState(sub)` の結果のみで `<FollowControl>` の表示と `initialFollowing` を決定。`followKey` は pending / ready-true / ready-false の 3 値で reseed。`timelineReady` ガードは撤去（フォロー判定とタイムライン取得を分離）。
- `src/routes/FollowControl.tsx`: `onFollowingChange` prop を新設し、`useFollowToggle` の楽観反映 / サーバ確定時に `useFollowState.setFollowing` へ書き戻すよう連結。

### Phase 2: アイコン / バナー画像アップロード
- `src/api/endpoints/images.ts` (新規): `uploadImage(client, file, signal?)` のみ。SNS backend `POST /v1/images` (multipart, field=`file`) に投げる。
- `src/hooks/useImageUpload.ts` (新規): `{ uploading, upload(file) }`。MIME を `image/jpeg|png|webp|gif` のホワイトリストで事前検証（`image/svg+xml` は Stored XSS 回避のため明示的に除外）、5MiB プレチェック、unmount 後の setState は `mountedRef` でガード。
- `src/routes/settings/SettingsProfileSection.tsx`:
  - 「アイコン画像」セクション新設。`useAuth().updateIcon(file)` (AuthCore 経由 `PUT /v1/user/icon`, field=`image`, JPEG/PNG/WebP, 5MiB) を呼び、`refreshMe()` で `/me` を再取得。1h TTL の旨は section 注釈と Toast に明示（強制 refresh は実装せず）。
  - バナーは「ファイルを選択」ボタンを追加（URL 入力欄の直前に配置）。アップロード成功で `bannerUrl` テキスト欄に `public_url` を流し込み、保存は既存の `handleProfileSubmit` に委譲する 2 段構成。**URL 直接入力欄は残置**。
  - 保存時に `isSafeHttpUrl` で `bannerUrl` を検証して `javascript:` / `data:` 等を弾く（表示時の `safeCssUrl` に二重で防御を入れる形）。
  - field 名・MIME 制約をアイコン (`image` / JPEG/PNG/WebP) とバナー (`file` / `image/*`) で取り違えないよう定数とコメントで明示。
  - 旧文言「アイコンも同様です」を撤去。

## 影響範囲・懸念点

- **影響範囲**: ユーザープロフィール画面（フォローボタンの判定経路）と設定画面（プロフィール編集セクション）。VM 層 / API 層の境界は維持しており、`api/types.ts` を UI から直接 import していない。
- **フォロワー数の初期表示は本タスクで触っていない**（計画書の決定事項メモどおり、別 feat に切り出し済み）。`useState<number | null>(null)` で初期 `-`、フォロー操作の楽観反映で更新する従来挙動を維持。
- **アイコン / バナーで責務が異なる**ことを計画書冒頭に詳細表でまとめてある。AuthCore (`PUT /v1/user/icon`, field=`image`, JPEG/PNG/WebP, 5MiB) と SNS backend (`POST /v1/images`, field=`file`, `image/*`, 5MiB) の取り違えに注意。
- **1h TTL の即時反映ずれ**: SNS backend の `IconURLCached` キャッシュ起因で、アイコンアップロード直後でも `/me` 経由の icon URL が古いままになることがある旨を UI 注釈と Toast に明示。強制 refresh / cache-bust は仕込んでいない（決定事項メモどおり）。
- **R2 無効環境**: ローカルで R2 を有効化していない場合、`/v1/images` がそもそも 404 になるためバナーアップロードが動かない。エラー時は Toast でユーザーに通知。

## その他

- 自動テストはこのリポジトリでは追加していない（`docs/tasks/remove-image-upload.md` 同様、テスト基盤未導入）。手動チェック観点は計画書 Phase 3 の項目で代替。
- `npm run lint`: 6 errors（全て `useAbortableResource.ts` / `useFollowToggle.ts` / `useLikeToggle.ts` / `usePagedList.ts` の **既存** 警告で、今回の差分には該当なし）。`npm run build`: 成功。
- 計画ドキュメント `docs/tasks/fix-follow-display-and-add-icon-banner-upload.md` も同梱（後続の参照用）。

### Motivation
- Provide a complete, enterprise-grade CI/CD and DevSecOps operating model for this Terraform-based EKS platform repository to enforce shift-left security, promotion gates, auditable plan/apply, drift detection, and GitOps integration.
- Supply concrete, copy-pasteable GitHub Actions workflow examples, `CODEOWNERS`, and an incident template so teams can rapidly adopt and harden pipeline governance.

### Description
- Added architecture documentation at `docs/cicd-devsecops-architecture.md` describing pipeline stages, approval/security gates, promotion and rollback strategies, release/versioning, artifact and GitOps integration.
- Added PR validation workflow at `.github/workflows/pr-validation.yml` that runs `terraform fmt -check -recursive`, `terraform init -backend=false`, `terraform validate`, `tflint`, `tfsec`, `checkov`, and uploads a PR plan artifact.
- Added multi-environment plan and apply workflows at `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml` and `.github/workflows/terraform-apply.yml` using OIDC credentials, per-environment plan artifacts, and GitHub Environments to enable production approvals.

body:
## Summary

- Add `adapters/go/sdk` as its own Go module with feature parity to the Python SDK
- Cover data publish, asset/relation CRUD via NATS request/reply, `platform.meta.*.changed` subscription, and an `Adapter` skeleton with device connect/reconnect hooks
- Three runnable examples mirror the Python ones (`temp_sensor`, `vibration_sensor`, `temp_sensor_with_recovery`) and ship inside the SDK module so they build without a workspace file

Closes #71

## Design notes

- **Separate go.mod** — SDK consumers pull only `nats.go`, not the core's heavier deps (sqlite, migrate, embedded `nats-server`)
- **Self-defined wire types + fixture round-trip tests** — `internal/core` cannot be imported externally; promoting those types to a public package is tracked separately
- **`Run(ctx)` + `Options` struct + `slog`** — signal handling stays in the caller via `signal.NotifyContext`, mirroring Go convention rather than the Python `BaseAdapter` pattern of grabbing SIGINT directly
- **`MetaChangeEvent.Before/After` as `json.RawMessage`** with `DecodeBefore` / `DecodeAfter` helpers — concrete type depends on `entity_type`

## Test plan

- [x] `cd adapters/go/sdk && go test ./...` — 38 tests pass (models round-trip, backoff, errors, client integration with embedded `nats-server`, adapter lifecycle)
- [x] `go test ./...` (root module) — no regressions in `cmd/core`, `internal/core`, `contexts`

### Motivation

- Replace brittle hard-coded graveyard jump routing with robust navmesh-driven pathing and add shortcuts for fall-through ledges to improve battleground pursuit and egress behavior.
- Allow longer path planning so bots commit to meaningful progress toward distant enemies instead of tiny local hops that get stuck on terrain.

### Description

- Removed the legacy `TryJumpOffWarsongGraveyard` routine and related special-case WSG fall-avoidance logic to rely on generalized navmesh routing.
- Increased battleground path calculation limit from `700.0f` to `2400.0f` and introduced `PLAYERBOT_BG_MOVEMENT_SEGMENT_DISTANCE`, `PLAYERBOT_BG_MIN_FALL_SHORTCUT_DROP`, and `PLAYERBOT_BG_FALL_SHORTCUT_COOLDOWN_MS` to tune segmenting and fall-shortcut behavior.
- Added `BuildNavPathSegmentDestination` to select a movement segment endpoint along the navmesh path and `TryBuildBattlegroundFallShortcutDestination` to probe safe ledge drops and apply a cooldown per-bot.
- Updated `TryBuildBattlegroundSegmentDestination` and `IssueMovePointThrottled` to prefer fall shortcuts, use the new path-segmentation, avoid reissuing movement while falling, and emit improved debug telemetry via `EmitBattlegroundGmDebug`.

### Testing

- Performed a full project build using `make`, and the build completed successfully.
- Ran the automated unit test suite via `ctest`, and all tests passed locally.

body:
# 🚀 Add new apps, curl-install script, and fix install state tracking

## 📋 Summary
Adds HAMRS and TrustedQSL as new installable apps, introduces a \`curl | bash\` remote install script so new users can bootstrap ham-apps in one command, fixes missing install-state tracking in three existing apps, and improves GUI sudo handling to prevent silent hangs.

## 🔧 Changes Made

**New apps**
- \`apps/hamrs/\` — AppImage-based portable logbook for POTA/Field Day; downloads from AWS S3, installs to \`/opt/hamrs/\`, creates wrapper and \`.desktop\` entry; handles x86_64, arm64, armv7l
- \`apps/trustedqsl/\` — builds tQSL 2.8.4 from source via CMake; tracks installed files via manifest for clean removal

**Remote install script**
- \`install.sh\` — self-contained \`curl | bash\` bootstrap; checks OS (Debian 11+/Ubuntu 20.04+), installs \`git\` and \`yad\`, clones the repo to \`~/ham-apps\`, idempotently adds ham-apps to PATH in \`~/.bashrc\` and \`~/.zshrc\`; supports \`--dry-run\` and \`--help\`; rejects paths with shell metacharacters (CWE-78 guard)

**Install state tracking fixes**
- \`apps/direwolf/install\` + \`uninstall\` — added missing \`mark_installed\`/\`mark_uninstalled\` calls; uninstall now also removes the \`.desktop\` file and handles apt-managed versions
- \`apps/wsjtx/install\` + \`uninstall\` — added missing \`mark_installed\`/\`mark_uninstalled\` calls
- \`apps/fldigi/install\` + \`uninstall\` — added missing \`mark_installed\`/\`mark_uninstalled\` calls

**GUI sudo handling** (\`gui/app-details\`)
- If sudo credentials are not cached, a yad password dialog now appears before the progress bar — no more silent hang waiting for terminal input
- Added a keepalive loop that refreshes the sudo timestamp every 60 s so long downloads/builds don't re-prompt mid-install

**Documentation and tests**
- \`README.md\` — added Quick Install one-liner section
- \`CLAUDE.md\` — added Commands section (run tests, shellcheck, smoke-test CLI) and How Tests Work section
- \`tests/test-install-sh\` — 15 tests covering OS checks, path validation, idempotency, PATH deduplication, and shellcheck compliance
- \`tests/test-hamrs-metadata\`, \`tests/test-hamrs-scripts\` — 30 tests covering metadata validity and script structure
- \`tests/test-trustedqsl-metadata\`, \`tests/test-trustedqsl-scripts\` — shellcheck and smoke tests for TrustedQSL

## 📁 Files Modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| \`install.sh\` | New — curl\|bash remote installer |
| \`apps/hamrs/*\` | New — 4 files |
| \`apps/trustedqsl/*\` | New — 4 files |
| \`apps/direwolf/install\` | Fix: add \`mark_installed\` |
| \`apps/direwolf/uninstall\` | Fix: add \`mark_uninstalled\`, remove \`.desktop\`, handle apt version |
| \`apps/wsjtx/install\` | Fix: add \`mark_installed\` |
| \`apps/wsjtx/uninstall\` | Fix: add \`mark_uninstalled\` |
| \`apps/fldigi/install\` | Fix: add \`mark_installed\` |
| \`apps/fldigi/uninstall\` | Fix: add \`mark_uninstalled\` |
| \`gui/app-details\` | Fix: GUI sudo prompt + keepalive |
| \`README.md\` | Add Quick Install section |

| \`tests/test-hamrs-*\` | New — test suite |
| \`tests/test-trustedqsl-*\` | New — test suite |
| \`docs/apps/index.md\` | Updated app catalogue |

## 🎯 Impact
Users can now install ham-apps with a single command. Two new apps are available for logbook (HAMRS) and LOTW upload (TrustedQSL). Existing apps correctly reflect installed/uninstalled state, and GUI installs no longer silently hang when sudo credentials expire.

## Summary

- Update y/x coords for mirror-flip orientations 2/3/4 in `read_to_array` so xarray label lookups land on the right pixel for georeferenced files.
- Cover both PixelIsArea (origin shifts by `N * step`) and PixelIsPoint (shifts by `(N-1) * step`).

## Context

PR #1521 added the buffer remap for the Orientation tag (274). The 5-8 axis-swap branch already updates the transform (and warns). See #1537 for a full reproducer.

author: joahg
body:
## What

Adds a third parser, `AgentTraceParser`, that consumes the open
[agent-trace.dev v1 spec](https://agent-trace.dev/) (`.agent-trace/*.json`
sidecars) and turns each `files[].conversations[].ranges[]` entry into
an `EditRecord`. Registered in `ParserRegistry::new()` ahead of the
existing Claude / Codex parsers and auto-discovered via a new
`get_agent_trace_dirs()` (`<cwd>/.agent-trace/`, `~/.agent-trace/`).

## Why

ai-blame today supports Claude Code and Codex/Copilot via bespoke
parsers per agent. The agent-trace.dev v1 spec is an open,
agent-agnostic JSON sidecar format intended exactly for this
attribution use case, so a single parser unlocks support for every
producer of the spec — first-party emitters or third-party exporters
that convert an agent's native logs — instead of growing the
parser-per-agent matrix forever.

## End-to-end smoke test

Ran against 21 real spec records validated against the upstream
[v1 schema](https://agent-trace.dev/schemas/v1/trace-record.json):

```text
$ ai-blame stats -t .agent-trace
Files with edits (all files): 41
Total successful edits: 126

$ ai-blame report -t .agent-trace
=== Summary ===
File                                               | Edits | First Edit       | Last Edit       
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
i18n.md                                            |     2 | 2026-04-13 16:28 | 2026-04-13 16:28

verify-nx-required-tasks.test.ts                   |     6 | 2026-05-08 22:30 | 2026-05-08 22:30

```

## Limitations (documented in the parser docstring + README)

agent-trace.dev records carry attribution **ranges + content_hash**
(spec §6.3) rather than raw `old_string` / `new_string` patches. As a
result:

| Command | Works on agent-trace records? |
|---|---|
| `stats`, `timeline`, `report`, `transcript` | ✅ Fully |
| `blame`, `annotate` | ⚠️ Marks touched lines but cannot do the patch-walk reconstruction the native parsers do |

A future iteration could use `content_hash` for position-independent
attribution — left as follow-up.

## Mapping

Each spec range becomes one `EditRecord`:

- `file_path` — `files[].path` (already repo-relative per spec).
- `timestamp` — record's top-level `timestamp` (per-revision, not per-edit).
- `model` — `contributor.model_id` (range override → conversation default → `unknown`).
- `session_id` — `conversation.url` → `related[type=session].url` → `unknown`.
- `agent_tool` / `agent_version` — record's top-level `tool` block.
- `is_create` / `change_size` — heuristic: ranges starting at line 1 are treated as create-shaped; `change_size` is the line span.

## Tests

7 new unit tests in `parsers::agent_trace::tests` covering parse
output, file-pattern filter, session-id fallback to `related[]`,
`can_parse` acceptance + rejection (incl. refusing to steal `.jsonl`
files from sibling parsers), and `collect_trace_files` extension
filtering.

author: sauravpanda
body:
Closes #61.

## Why

`DanceClip.assetIdentifier` points at a `PHAsset` `localIdentifier`. If the user deletes the source video from Photos (or the asset becomes unresolvable for any other reason — iCloud cycling, corruption, library reset), every annotation we've persisted around it — segments, beat times, downbeat anchor, notes, tags — silently orphans. The metadata is durable in SwiftData; the underlying media is not. That's also a non-starter for the planned CloudKit sync (#55), which needs a stable local source of truth on each device.

## What changed

- **`OriginalImportService` + `OriginalStorage`** — new service mirroring the existing trim machinery. Sandbox path is `Documents/Originals/<uuid>.<ext>`. Same rationale as `TrimStorage`: not `tmp/`, not `caches/`, so the OS can't reclaim mid-practice and the file survives reboot.
- **`DanceClip.originalFileName` + `originalFileURL` + `preferredLocalFileURL`** — optional field so existing clips migrate cleanly. `preferredLocalFileURL` returns `trim ?? original`, used by `PracticeView` and the trim-onDismiss reload path.
- **`LibraryView.importOne`** — copies bytes after `resolveAVAsset`. Wrapped in `try?` so a clip still imports with PHAsset-only fallback if the copy fails (e.g. weird HEIC video resource shapes), instead of blocking the user.
- **`LibraryView.commitDelete`** — cleans up sandboxed originals + trims when a clip is deleted, so we don't leak per-clip bytes into `Documents/`.
- **`PracticeView`** — passes `preferredLocalFileURL` to the player VM. No-op for legacy clips (still resolves via PHAsset), durable for new ones.
- **Bonus**: removed a duplicate `SegmentList` row in `PracticeView` that rendered patterns twice (leftover from an earlier merge).

## Tradeoff

Storage roughly doubles per imported clip (Photos copy + ours). For a personal-use library of dance clips it's fine; if it ever becomes a problem we can add a per-clip "don't own bytes" toggle.

## Out of scope

- Migrating existing PHAsset-only clips. The simplest path forward is just to re-import. A future PR can add a one-shot batch migration.
- CloudKit asset sync — separate work (#55), but this change is a precondition.

## Tests

86/86 pass (was 76). Added:
- 5 `OriginalImportServiceTests` covering storage paths, byte-identical copy, extension preservation, default-extension fallback, missing-source error.
- 3 `ModelsTests` covering `preferredLocalFileURL` priority (trim > original) and nil fallthrough for legacy clips.

author: dazwin
body:
**Stacked on #43** (`fix/relay-config-opt-in`). The first commit here is #43's commit; rebases away cleanly once #43 lands.

PR #43 added two new config fields — `force_private` and `trusted_relays` — that decide which peers a NATed node uses to obtain a relay circuit. Once a user configures them, it's useful to see at a glance which of the currently-connected peers actually come from those settings, without cross-referencing peer IDs against the config file by hand.

This PR makes `kwaainet p2p peers list` do that visualisation:

- **Tag trusted relays** as `(trusted relay)` in gold (256-color 220), parallel to the existing cyan `(bootstrap)` tag added in #42.
- **Colour the connection-kind bracket**: green `[direct]`, yellow `[ relay]`. Kind is now classified through a small `ConnKind` enum rather than a bool, so future kinds (e.g. `[ holed]` for a hole-punch upgrade detection) can slot in without disturbing call sites.
- **Sort the rows**: bootstraps first, then trusted relays, then plain direct, then via-relay; within each group, by peer ID. Stable across polls so a `watch -n 2` loop doesn't churn.
- **Extend the summary line** with a `trusted relay(s)` count alongside `bootstrap peer(s)`.

### Why 256-color for gold

The standard 16-colour palette has no orange/gold — closest is yellow, which is already used for `[ relay]`. Going 256-color (`\x1b[38;5;220m`) gives a distinct gold. Every modern terminal supports 256-color (iTerm2, kitty, alacritty, gnome-terminal, Terminal.app, Windows Terminal), so the compatibility risk is essentially zero. Inline ANSI keeps us off the dep treadmill — if colour use spreads beyond two strings, that's the time to pull in a colour crate.

### Verified

- `cargo build --package kwaainet --bin kwaainet` clean
- `cargo fmt --check` on the changed file: clean
- Manual smoke against a live local daemon: `(bootstrap)` and `(trusted relay)` tags render correctly; sort order stable across `watch`-style repeat invocations.

author: jagobainda
body:
### Problem
Several tRPC endpoints had no server-side rate limit, making them viable DoS vectors. Any authenticated client connecting directly over WebSocket could bypass the official client's UI flow and call them in a tight loop, generating thousands of SQLite queries per second against a single-writer database.

### Fix
Wrap each affected endpoint with the existing `rateLimitedProcedure` infrastructure. All limits are added to `config.rateLimiters.*` so they can be tuned via `config.ini` without touching code.

| Endpoint | Limit (per IP) | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `messages.signalTyping` | 40 / 5 s | Legitimate max at `TYPING_MS = 300 ms` is ~16/5 s. Cap gives ~2.5× headroom and accounts for multiple typists behind a shared NAT. |
| `messages.getMessages` | 60 / 10 s | Heaviest read endpoint (~7 queries + JOINs + pubsub). Cap comfortably covers rapid channel-switching and scroll pagination. |
| `messages.toggleMessageReaction` | 60 / 10 s | 4 queries per call; same threat profile as `signalTyping`. |
| `channels.markAsRead` | 60 / 10 s | 3 queries per call; triggered naturally by channel-switching. |
| `dms.openDirectMessage` | 10 / 60 s | Creates persistent state + publishes permission events; called at most a few times per session legitimately. |
| `emojis.addEmoji` | 10 / 60 s | Loops on `fileManager.saveFile` + DB insert per array element with no upper bound; admin-gated but still unbounded. |
| `others.handshake` | 10 / 60 s | Only `publicProcedure` — reachable pre-auth with no prior limit. |

The chosen rates are a starting point and may need tuning in real deployments, particularly for the navigation endpoints on servers where many users share an IP. Treat them as debatable.

Some unprotected endpoints were intentionally left out: those gated behind admin permissions (limited blast radius), low-cost single-lookup queries (not worth the noise), and endpoints whose cost lives inside a delegated subsystem where the right place to throttle isn't the tRPC layer.

Closes #722

Fixes #79844.

## Problem
When a user message is sent with an `idempotencyKey`, that key is persisted on the transcript message but only surfaces as a top-level message field on hydration. Clients consuming `chat.history` (and the SSE inline stream) expect identity-style metadata to live inside the `__openclaw` envelope alongside `seq`, `id`, `importedFrom`, etc., so they can correlate echoed messages without sniffing top-level fields.

## Change
Hoist the persisted `idempotencyKey` into the `__openclaw` envelope at hydration time:
- `parsedSessionEntryToMessage` in `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts` — covers `chat.history` full reads and recent-tail reads.
- `SessionHistorySseState.appendInlineMessage` in `src/gateway/session-history-state.ts` — covers the live inline SSE append.
- `broadcastSessionMessage` in `src/gateway/server-session-events.ts` — covers the inline broadcast path.

The original top-level `idempotencyKey` field is preserved on the message object for back-compat, so existing readers do not regress.

## Tests
- `src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts` — new test verifies `idempotencyKey` surfaces on both full and recent-tail reads, and is absent when the persisted message has no key.
- `src/gateway/session-history-state.test.ts` — new test verifies inline-append surfaces `idempotencyKey` in `__openclaw` alongside `id`/`seq`.

author: szhekpisov
body:
## What

Add `--html-output <path>`: writes a single self-contained HTML mutation report. The page bundles the [Stryker `mutation-testing-elements`](https://github.com/stryker-mutator/mutation-testing-elements) web component (3.7.3, vendored under `internal/report/assets/`) plus the Stryker v2 JSON payload into one file. Open in any browser — no web server, no network access, no companion JSON file.

## Why

`--stryker-output` already produces the right JSON, but viewing it requires either (a) shipping the file alongside an HTML viewer, or (b) publishing to the Stryker Dashboard. Neither works for air-gapped CI or for "click the artifact link in a PR check" workflows. A single self-contained HTML file solves both: drop it as a CI artifact, link to it from the check, click and read.

The dashboard (with history + hosted badge) is still preferable when you can use it; the README points users there first and frames `--html-output` as the local / air-gapped option.

## How

- `WriteStryker` is split: a new `buildStrykerReport` returns the in-memory Stryker v2 struct, and `WriteStryker` / `WriteHTML` both consume it. No duplicated mapping logic.
- `WriteHTML` (`internal/report/html.go`) renders a `text/template` with two fields: the `go:embed`'d JS bundle and the marshaled JSON. `text/template` (not `html/template`) is used deliberately — `html/template` would HTML-escape the embedded JS and JSON. Both fields are placed inside `<script>` blocks where HTML entity escaping does not apply, and `json.Marshal`'s default `<`/`>`/`&` escaping keeps `</script>` substrings inside report data inert.
- Tests pin the round-trip, the headline self-contained property (no `<script src=` / `<link ` / `<iframe ` in the static chrome), an error-propagation case, and the `</script>`-in-source escape behavior.
- Vendored bundle refresh procedure documented in `internal/report/assets/README.md`.

## Checklist

- [x] PR title follows convention (`feat:`)
- [x] `go test -race ./...` passes locally
- [x] `go vet ./...` and `golangci-lint run` clean
- [x] New/changed behavior covered by tests (`html_test.go`: round-trip, self-contained, error propagation, embedded-JSON safety)
- [ ] Coverage threshold met (`./internal/...` ≥ 97.6%) — to be verified in CI
- [ ] Mutation efficacy threshold met on changed lines (`gomutants --changed-since main ./internal/...` = 100%) — to be verified in CI
- [x] No new Go module dependencies. The vendored 228 KB JS bundle (`mutation-test-elements.js`, MIT-licensed UMD build of `mutation-testing-elements@3.7.3`) is checked in under `internal/report/assets/` and embedded via `go:embed`; refresh procedure documented in `assets/README.md`.

## Notes for reviewers

- The vendored JS bundle is ~228 KB and dominates the diff size; it lives under `internal/report/assets/` so it's easy to skip during review.
- The page assigns `el.report = JSON.parse(data)` from a `<script type="application/json">` block; this avoids a second escape-pass through JS string literals.
- Consider as a follow-up: a one-line guard test asserting the embedded JS bundle contains no literal `</script` sequence. The current 3.7.3 bundle is clean; the test would catch a future bundle refresh that introduces one and would silently break the page.
