  - RAW byte-count and shape checks
  - explicit phase and voxel-size convention
  - BV/TV and slice-wise heterogeneity analysis
  - projected bone thickness maps
  - surface-based morphometry proxies
  - distance-transform and local-thickness/separation summaries
  - connected-component and percolation checks
  - axis-aligned chord-length distributions
  - static PyVista split-plane 3D visualization
  - optional marrow-space pore-network extraction hook

- Expanded public docs:
  - detailed morphometry API documentation with definition, equations, algorithm steps, unit conversion, backend method choices, assumptions, limitations, and verification scope
  - example-data provenance for the trabecular image
  - updated agent documentation so future scientific API docs include calculation details rather than wrapper-level summaries

## Scientific Notes

- The local-thickness API is phase-general: callers provide the binary phase mask to measure, and `voids` does not infer the physical meaning of image labels.
- The API returns diameter values, not radii: `T = 2 h R`, where `h` is isotropic voxel size and `R` is the backend radius-like local-thickness output.
- Current local-thickness support requires isotropic voxel spacing.
- The tests validate the `voids` API contract and unit conversion around the external PoreSpy backend; they are not an independent validation of PoreSpy’s local-thickness implementation.

## Data / Reproducibility Note

The notebook expects:

`examples/data/trabecular-image/Trabecular_300_cubo_0_poro_1_osso_2086nm.raw`

At the time this PR description was prepared, that RAW file existed locally but was still untracked.

## Summary
- Extends `cmake/lua_codegen/` (T-106) to handle Lua system bodies. Captures `IRSystem.registerSystem({...})` calls, slices the tick function source via `lua_getinfo`, parses the DSL subset from #587, and emits typed `IRSystem::createSystem<...>` calls.
- Hand-rolled Lua-flavored lexer + recursive-descent parser + type-tracked C++ emitter live in two new files (`system_dsl.{hpp,cpp}`). Strict-error contract — out-of-DSL constructs reject at build time pointing at file:line:feature.
- Intrinsic whitelist registry maps Lua `math.*` / `IRMath.*` calls to `IRMath::*` (per the no-std-math-outside-engine/math/ rule). Adding an intrinsic = one line.

## Stack context
Stacked on: https://github.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/pull/596 (T-106)
Full chain: T-105 → T-106 → T-107

## DSL subset
Allowed: canonical `for i = 0, arch.length - 1 do` loop; column ops `arch.Comp:at(i)` / `:setAt(i, v)` / `:getField(i, "f")` / `:setField(i, "f", v)` on Lua-defined components; `Comp.new(...)` constructors; `+ - * / %`, comparisons, `and/or/not`, `if/elseif/else`; `local` decls; whitelisted intrinsics. Forbidden: closures with external upvalues, metatables, dynamic dispatch, `require`, table constructors beyond `Comp.new`, `while`/`repeat`/`break`/`goto`, nested function defs, varargs, `nil`, `_` length op, `^` exponent, multi-target locals, multi-step for-loops, generic-for, dynamic field names. Each rejection emits a clear file:line:feature error.

## v1 scope notes
- Per-system `mode='codegen'`/`mode='eval'` override is **T-108**. Until then, files passed to `irreden_lua_codegen()` must contain only CODEGEN-translatable systems.
- CODEGEN bodies use only Lua-defined components. Systems referencing C++-bound types stay in the EVAL path.
- `SystemName` enum partial generation is deferred — codegen systems register via `IRSystem::createSystem<...>` directly, producing valid `SystemId`s in the same id space.

author: jasonherald
body:
## Summary

- Ports the dbdexter `meteor_demod` reference (the same algorithm SatDump uses) to give the LRPT pipeline a proper OQPSK demod path. Current METEOR-M2 satellites (M2-3, M2-4) all transmit Offset QPSK at 72 ksym/s — Q delayed by Tsym/2 from I — and our previously-hardcoded standard-QPSK pipeline can lock onto OQPSK signals but produces sub-quality soft symbols (Gardner timing recovery's error metric assumes I and Q are co-timed, exactly the assumption OQPSK breaks). That's the strongest suspect for the silent-Meteor-pass debug arc this session.
- The new path lives in two modules under `crates/sdr-dsp/src/lrpt/`: `meteor_pll.rs` (Costas with separate `mix_i` / `mix_q` mixes, lock detection via EMA-of-error, free-run frequency sweep through ±fmax) and `mm_timing.rs` (Mueller-Muller timing with the dual-rail `advance_timeslot_dual` state machine — state 1 = I-tick mid-symbol, state 2 = Q-tick at the symbol boundary). `LrptDemod` dispatches between QPSK (existing SDR++-style Costas + Gardner) and OQPSK (new dbdexter chain) via a new `LrptMode` enum. The QPSK path is unchanged — no regression risk for legacy METEOR-M N2 archival recordings.
- Catalog now carries `KnownSatellite::lrpt_modulation: Option<LrptModulation>`; M2-3 and M2-4 are flagged `Oqpsk`. New `UiToDsp::SetLrptModulation` message routes the catalog-derived modulation from the wiring layer (window.rs auto-record arm) through to the DSP thread, which builds the appropriate inner chain on lazy decoder init.

## Algorithm choices (why dbdexter, not SDR++)

I started with SDR++'s OQPSK implementation (just a 1-sample delay on Q post-Costas, then standard Mueller-Muller) but its source has a `// TODO: Additional 1/24th sample delay` comment acknowledging the integer-sample delay leaves a fractional residual the timing loop never recovers. That matches the SDR++ community reputation: standard QPSK Meteors decode fine, OQPSK Meteors are marginal, "use SatDump or dbdexter for serious M2-3/M2-4 work."

The dbdexter approach is structurally different: instead of re-aligning the signal then using single-rail timing, it samples I and Q at their actual Tsym/2-offset instants via the dual-tick state machine, mixes each rail independently through `pll_mix_i` / `pll_mix_q`, and runs Mueller-Muller on the Q rail only. Combined with a much tighter PLL bandwidth (1 Hz vs SDR++'s ~720 Hz) plus a free-run frequency sweep that scans ±0.15 rad through the carrier-offset range until lock, it locks on signals that SDR++'s tuning sits on top of without ever locking.

Tuning per dbdexter `meteor_demod/demod.h`: `PLL_BW = 1` Hz, `SYM_BW = 0.00005`, `FREQ_MAX = 0.3` rad/call (halved for OQPSK).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p sdr-dsp lrpt::` — 31 tests pass, including 3 new ones exercising the OQPSK pipeline on synthetic 2-sps interleaved I/Q
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace -- -D warnings` — clean (matches CI invocation)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --locked` — clean
- [x] `cargo bench -p sdr-dsp --bench lrpt_demod --no-run` — both QPSK and OQPSK benches compile (existing `lrpt_demod_1s_144ksps` bench renamed to `_qpsk_` and a parallel `_oqpsk_` bench added so future regressions in either path are catchable)
- [x] `make install CARGO_FLAGS="--release --features whisper-cuda"` succeeds; binary contains the new `LRPT modulation set to` log marker
- [ ] **(user)** Smoke against a recorded Meteor IQ: select METEOR-M2 4 in the satellites panel, confirm the log shows `LRPT modulation set to Oqpsk` followed by `LRPT decoder initialised at 144000 Hz IF rate, modulation = Oqpsk`, and watch for image rows in the LRPT viewer
- [ ] **(user)** Regression smoke: tune to a strong local FM station, confirm audio still works (controller wiring touched)

Closes #662

author: mannism
body:
## Summary

- **Per-call `timeoutMs` override** — `LlmCallOptions.timeoutMs` overrides `config.timeoutMs` per attempt; each retry gets a fresh deadline
- **Caller `AbortSignal`** — `LlmCallOptions.signal` propagates to the SDK (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Perplexity) or wins a `Promise.race` (Gemini); `kind:'cancelled'`, never retried
- **Stream stall detection** — `LlmCallOptions.streamStallTimeoutMs` fires a per-chunk timer via `withStallTimeout`; `kind:'stream_stall'`, never retried (partial output)
- **`LlmError.kind` discriminator** — new `LlmErrorKind`: `cancelled | timeout | stream_stall | http | network | unknown`
- All 5 providers fully wired. Gemini uses `Promise.race` with documented socket-leak caveat (no native SDK signal support); `httpOptions.timeout = configMs * 2` backstop.
- New `abort.ts` module: `createAttemptController`, `cancellableSleep`, `withStallTimeout`, `classifyAbort`

## Test plan

- [x] 244 unit tests (was 202, +42) — `pnpm test` passes across all packages
- [x] Typecheck clean — `pnpm typecheck` passes with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`
- [x] Build clean — `pnpm build` produces clean `dist/`
- [x] Live smoke — all 3 v0.3.0 cases pass:

```
===== v0.3.0 ABORT / TIMEOUT / STALL SMOKE =====

--- Case (a): timeoutMs:1 per-call override (expect kind:timeout) ---
PASS  kind:timeout  retryable:true

--- Case (b): pre-aborted AbortSignal (expect kind:cancelled) ---
PASS  kind:cancelled  retryable:false

--- Case (c): Perplexity stream() with streamStallTimeoutMs:50 ---
PASS (stall detected as expected with 50ms window)  kind:stream_stall

========== smoke complete ==========
```

## PR Comprehension Gate

1. **What does this change do?** Adds three cancellation mechanisms to `llm-client` — deadline timeout, caller abort, and stream stall — across all 5 providers, with a typed `LlmError.kind` discriminator for downstream branching.

2. **What fails silently?** Nothing new. The Gemini socket-leak is documented — when the internal controller aborts, the SDK HTTP request continues until `httpOptions.timeout` (2× configured timeout) fires. This is best-effort; flagged in module JSDoc and README.

3. **What's the blast radius?** All 5 providers updated. The `LlmCallOptions` interface gains 3 optional fields — non-breaking. `normalizeThrownError` gains `kind` on all error paths — consumers checking `instanceof LlmError` still work; `kind` is additive. The `retry.ts` backoff now uses `cancellableSleep` which resolves early on signal — consistent with the caller's expectation that a cancelled call returns immediately.

4. **Why these dependencies?** No new runtime dependencies. `abort.ts` is hand-rolled signal composition to avoid `AbortSignal.any` (requires Node ≥22.0.0); we target Node ≥20.

5. **What's the abort reason source?** `classifyAbort` uses `ctl.abortReason()` (the `AttemptController`) as the authoritative source — not `err.name`. This is required because Anthropic's SDK throws `APIUserAbortError` (not `'AbortError'`) when a signal fires. The controller's reason is always correct; error names are not.

6. **Fake timer test pattern?** `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(ms)` (async variant) — not `vi.advanceTimersByTime`. `Promise.race()` involves microtask scheduling; the async variant flushes both fake timers and pending microtasks so races resolve correctly. Documented in `abort.test.ts` header.

## Key design decisions (Owner pre-ratified)

- Gemini: `Promise.race` only — no native signal. Socket-leak bounded to 2× configured timeout.
- `streamStallTimeoutMs` defaults 30 000 ms, independent of `timeoutMs` — tolerant of reasoning-model think-pauses.
- Hand-rolled signal composition (no `AbortSignal.any`) — maintains Node ≥20 compatibility.
- `mergeRetryOptsWithSignal` helper for `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` compatibility.
- `classifyAbort` ordering: runs on raw SDK error BEFORE `normalizeXxxError` — essential for correct kind on Anthropic `APIUserAbortError`.

Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ convict (6.2.4 → 6.2.5) · [Repo](https://github.com/mozilla/node-convict) · [Changelog](https://github.com/mozilla/node-convict/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Convict has prototype pollution via load(), loadFile(), and schema initialization

Impact

Two unguarded prototype pollution paths exist, not covered by previous fixes:

  1. config.load() / config.loadFile() — overlay() recursively merges config data without checking for forbidden keys. Input containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype (e.g. from a JSON file) causes the recursion to reach Object.prototype and write attacker-controlled values onto it.
  2. Schema initialization — passing a schema with constructor.prototype.* keys to convict({...}) causes default-value propagation to write directly to Object.prototype at startup.

Depending on how polluted properties are consumed, impact ranges from unexpected behavior to authentication bypass or RCE.

Workarounds

Do not pass untrusted data to load(), loadFile(), or convict().

Resources

Prior advisory: GHSA-44fc-8fm5-q62h
Related issue: #423

🚨 Convict has Prototype Pollution via startsWith() function

Summary

A prototype pollution vulnerability exists in the latest version of the convict npm package (6.2.4). Despite a previous fix that attempted to mitigate prototype pollution by checking whether user input started with a forbidden key, it is still possible to pollute Object.prototype via a crafted input using String.prototype.

Details

The vulnerability resides in line 564 of https://github.com/mozilla/node-convict/blob/master/packages/convict/src/main.js where startsWith() function is used to check whether user provided input contain forbidden strings.

PoC

Steps to reproduce

  1. Install latest version of convict using npm install or cloning from git
  2. Run the following code snippet:
String.prototype.startsWith = () => false; 
const convict = require('convict');
let obj = {};
const config = convict(obj);
console.log({}.polluted);
config.set('constructor.prototype.polluted', 'yes');
console.log({}.polluted);    // prints yes -> the patch is bypassed and prototype pollution occurred

Expected behavior

Prototype pollution should be prevented and {} should not gain new properties.
This should be printed on the console:

undefined
undefined OR throw an Error

Actual behavior

Object.prototype is polluted
This is printed on the console:

undefined 
yes

Impact

This is a prototype pollution vulnerability, which can have severe security implications depending on how convict is used by downstream applications. Any application that processes attacker-controlled input using convict.set may be affected.
It could potentially lead to the following problems:

  1. Authentication bypass
  2. Denial of service
  3. Remote code execution (if polluted property is passed to sinks like eval or child_process)

author: iifawzi
body:
Three log sites used to capture the entire message body — RunMQ.publish on success, RunMQFailureLoggerProcessor on every per-attempt failure, and RunMQRetriesCheckerProcessor.logMaxRetriesReached on DLQ-bound messages. For megabyte-sized payloads at high throughput, structured-log transports JSON.stringify those refs even when the level filters the line out, allocating GB/s of garbage the GC has to reclaim.

Drop the payload from those log lines and add correlationId + messageId instead — both are cheap strings RunMQ already attaches to every message. The actual body is still recoverable via the broker (retry queues hold mid-flight messages; DLQ holds the original AMQP body verbatim per #25), keyed by those same ids.

Add an opt-in RunMQConnectionConfig.logFullMessagePayload flag for debug scenarios where you want the body inline.

body:
Ports the React preview UX improvements from PRs #3 / #4 / #5 into the actual Shopify-uploadable Liquid theme. After this lands, the .zip merchants upload to Shopify Admin behaves the same way as the React preview.

## What changed

### Cart UX (`assets/theme.js`)
Old: \`document.addEventListener('cart:added', open)\` — the cart drawer opened on top of whatever the customer was looking at the moment they added something.
New: a top-right toast (\`Added <product-name> to cart 🛒\`) surfaces and dismisses on its own; the cart drawer only opens when the customer clicks the cart icon. The badge still updates live via \`Cart.subscribe\`.

### Generic site-wide toast (`layout/theme.liquid` + `assets/theme.css` + `assets/theme.js`)
New \`[data-app-toast]\` element in the layout, \`.app-toast\` CSS, and a \`window.theme.toast(msg, opts)\` helper. The wishlist page keeps its own \`[data-wishlist-toast]\` for wishlist-only messages.

### Email Support button (`sections/faq.liquid` + delegated handler in `theme.js`)
Click → still tries the \`mailto:\` link AND copies \`support@mollyandsophie.com\` to the clipboard AND fires a confirmation toast. Users without a default mail client get visible feedback instead of a button that looks dead. Driven by \`[data-app-mailto]\` so any mailto button in the theme can opt in by adding the attribute.

### Donation Impact section removed (`templates/index.json`)
The \"Real Impact, Real Receipts\" stats block (\`$4,287 / 12 / 8,341 / 100%\`) is gone from both the sections map and the order array. The numbers were placeholder; the company is brand new and can't claim those totals yet. The Giving Back section that explains the 1%-to-rescues model is unchanged. The \`donation-impact.liquid\` section file is intentionally left in place so it remains an option in the theme editor for later.

### Real Results graph section (new — `snippets/product-test-results.liquid`)
Server-side SVG line chart, rendered at the bottom of every product page. \"Molly & Sophie\" (winning) vs a \"Leading brand\" (declining) on a category-relevant metric. Points are precomputed in Liquid so there's no runtime JS. Copy varies per category:

| Category | Y-axis | X-axis | Headline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treats | Freshness % | Days after opening | Stays soft, stays fresh. |
| Beds | Comfort score | Hours of sleep | Pressure-relieving from minute one. |
| Toys | Squeaks remaining | Play sessions | Survives the zoomies. |
| Walks/Harness | Pull reduction % | Walks | No-pull that actually pulls less. |

## Already in the theme — no port needed

While inventorying I confirmed these were already in the Shopify theme and didn't need porting:
- ✅ Promo popup show-once (uses \`localStorage.msPromoDismissed\`)
- ✅ Wishlist drawer with toasts (\`Wishlist.toast\`)
- ✅ Bundle + FAQ inside the gallery column on the PDP
- ✅ Gallery thumbnail click swaps the main image (no lightbox interception)

## Verification

- ✅ All 14 JSON files validate (\`node -e \"JSON.parse(...)\"\`)
- ✅ Liquid tag balance: opens === closes on every modified file
- ✅ \`node --check assets/theme.js\` — no syntax errors
- ✅ Theme zip rebuilt successfully (6.42 MB, 80 files, includes \`snippets/product-test-results.liquid\`)

author: daniella-melo
body:
### Changelog:
Antes da refatoração, as páginas do chat e do admin faziam tudo misturado — a mesma página que mostrava os botões e mensagens na tela também acessava o banco de dados, processava a lógica de navegação da árvore de decisão, e construía URLs do WhatsApp. Era como se um garçom também cozinhasse, lavasse a louça e fizesse o caixa.

### As novas peças criadas
1. DTOs (Data Transfer Objects) - dtos.py
- São "envelopes" de dados que viajam do backend pro frontend
- São imutáveis (ninguém pode alterar os dados acidentalmente)
- Como formulários preenchidos que só podem ser lidos, nunca rabiscados

2. ChatService - chat_service.py
- É o "gerente" do chatbot
- Sabe fazer tudo: navegar pela árvore, processar o que o usuário digitou, voltar, reiniciar, gerar URL do WhatsApp, salvar feedback
- Mas não sabe nada sobre visual — ele só entrega dados prontos (os DTOs)

3. AdminService - admin_service.py
- É o "gerente" da página de administração
- Busca os feedbacks do banco e formata pra exibição
- Também não sabe nada sobre visual

4. ChatRenderer - chat_renderer.py
- É o "artista" — só sabe desenhar na tela
- Recebe os DTOs e callbacks (tipo "quando clicarem aqui, faça isso")
- Não sabe nada sobre banco de dados ou lógica de negócio

### O que mudou nos arquivos existentes
#### chat.py (página do chat)
- Antes: importava 7+ classes diferentes (engine, sessão, processador, banco, etc.)
- Depois: importa só ChatService + ChatRenderer. Ficou muito mais simples.
#### admin.py (página admin)
- Antes: acessava o banco de dados diretamente
- Depois: usa só o AdminService
#### whatsapp_redirect.py
- Removido o método que renderizava botão na tela (isso agora é responsabilidade do ChatRenderer)
- Ficou só com a função de construir a URL

### Observações
Se alguém quiser mudar o visual, mexe só no ChatRenderer, sem risco de quebrar a lógica
Se alguém quiser mudar a lógica (ex: trocar banco de dados), mexe só no Service, sem risco de quebrar a tela
